items.defectStatement: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` matches a submitted address with the exact, case-sensitive query `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` (no normalization of `email`), and emails are never downcased before being stored on BlockedEmail or passed through `User.new_from_params`. On a case-sensitive database (Discourse's PostgreSQL), a record blocked as `bad@spammers.org` will not match a signup as `Bad@Spammers.org`, letting the blocked address bypass the email validator's block.
obligations: should_block?(email) must find a matching BlockedEmail record regardless of the case of the submitted address, including case differences in the local part (not only the domain).

The matching normalization must be consistent with how BlockedEmail records are stored/normalized, so that a record saved with mixed case is still found by the lookup (and any new records saved are normalized the same way).

Preserve existing behavior: return a falsy value when no record matches; when a record matches, increment match_count, set last_match_at, and save the record; return true only when the record's action_type is :block (and false for :do_nothing).

Do not break existing callers/signatures: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) with the raw email, and the method stays a class method returning a boolean; handle nil/blank input without raising.
items.notes: The finding's suggested fix (case-insensitive lookup such as `where('lower(email) = ?', email.to_s.downcase)` plus storing blocked emails lower-case) is valid, but an equally valid alternative is to normalize the address inside should_block? and on save; the grader should accept either as long as lookup and storage normalization are consistent. Trap: `Email.downcase` (lib/email.rb) only lowercases the DOMAIN and preserves the local part, so a fix that only applies Email.downcase on one side still leaves a local-part case bypass. Also note the unique index (`add_index :blocked_emails, :email, unique: true`) and `validates :email, uniqueness: true` are exact/case-sensitive, so if a fix starts lowercasing stored addresses it should also consider case-insensitive uniqueness to avoid duplicate blocked entries — but that is secondary to the bypass being fixed. The finding is slightly overstated for MySQL (default case-insensitive collation would already match); it is a real defect on PostgreSQL.

items.defectStatement: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, every username from the comma-separated list is passed to group.add(user) without checking current membership or deduplicating the input. Group#add pushes onto the has_many :through :users association (app/models/group.rb:272-274), which inserts a group_users row immediately, and the DB has a unique index on group_users (group_id, user_id) (db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9), so adding an existing member or repeating a username raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique instead of being a no-op. Because each push is saved on its own with no transaction, a failure part-way through the loop can also leave earlier additions committed.
obligations: Adding a username that is already a member of the group must succeed idempotently (no RecordNotUnique, no duplicate group_users row, and the request still renders success_json).
A username repeated more than once in the comma-separated usernames parameter must be added only once and must not raise.

Existing behavior must be preserved: unknown usernames are skipped without error, automatic groups still return the can_not_modify_automatic 422 response, and valid new members are added so that group.users reflects them.
If any addition fails, membership must not be left partially applied (all additions for the request either committed or none).
items.notes: The cited text is accurate; the unique index and Group#add push behavior are confirmed. A minimal valid fix is skipping users whose id is already in group.user_ids (careful: user_ids on the through association may be cached after a push, so a local accumulator or reload may be needed) and/or wrapping the loop in a transaction; either approach satisfies the obligations. Do not require a specific implementation. remove_member has an analogous but non-raising concern (deleting a non-member is a no-op) and is out of scope for this finding.

items.defectStatement: `totalPages` in app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 (lines 11-14) computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1, so `currentPage === totalPages` (and thus `showingLast`) is false on the real last page, the `next` action is not blocked there, and the pager can advance to offset == user_count where it renders an empty page labelled "2/2".
obligations: totalPages must equal the ceiling of user_count / limit, so exact multiples are not overcounted (50/50 -> 1, 25/50 -> 1, 0/50 -> 0, 51/50 -> 2, 100/50 -> 2).
totalPages must still return 0 when user_count is 0.
totalPages must remain a computed property that depends on both limit and user_count so it recomputes when either changes.

With the corrected totalPages, showingLast (currentPage === totalPages) must be true on the real last page (e.g. offset 0 with user_count 50 and limit 50), so the `next` action is a no-op and no empty page is reachable.
items.notes: The cited lines are only totalPages; currentPage (floor(offset/limit)+1) is correct for zero-based offsets and should not be changed. The finding's extra suggestion to guard `next` (stop when offset + limit >= user_count) is not in the cited lines and is largely redundant once totalPages is ceil: showingLast already gates `next` at the last page. Note Discourse.Group.findMembers already clamps offset to user_count, so offset can never exceed user_count. Valid fix forms: `return Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"));` (the zero guard may be kept or dropped since ceil(0)=0), as long as the computed property declaration and dependencies are preserved.

items.defectStatement: In the public group members route, setupController now calls `model.findMembers()`, which requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with the group's default `limit` of 50 and `offset` 0 (see models/group.js and GroupsController#members, which caps at `params[:limit] || 50`). The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders only `members` with no pagination/load-more controls and no action to change `offset`, so members past the first 50 are unreachable in the public view. Previously the members list was populated differently and the public view could show all members (the admin side, by contrast, has next/previous actions).
obligations: The public group members view must be able to reach members beyond the first page (default 50): either by adding pagination/load-more controls that change the group's offset/limit and re-call findMembers, or by fetching all members for the public view.

Initial load must still work: navigating to group.members must still set the group controller's `showing` to 'members', set the route controller's model to the group, and populate the group's `members` (e.g. via `model.findMembers()`), so groups with <=50 members are unaffected.

Any pagination state introduced must respect the group's `limit`/`offset`/`user_count` (offset clamped to [0, user_count], limit > 0) and must not issue requests with an out-of-range offset or produce a page counter that breaks when user_count is 0.
Existing behavior for callers of `findMembers()` (admin group route/controller, removeMember/addMembers reloads) and the existing admin test expectations must not be broken.
items.notes: The admin side already implements the intended pattern: admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6 has next/previous actions that set `offset = min(offset+limit, user_count)` / `max(offset-limit, 0)` and call `group.findMembers()`, plus currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast and a pagination UI in admin/templates/group.hbs; a valid fix can mirror that in the public group controller/template. Alternative valid fixes: request all members from the public route/serializer (server-side change), or add a load-more action in group/members.hbs. Notes/traps: (1) `findMembers()` resolves to undefined (the .then callback does not return the result), so no caller can rely on the promise value; the members are exposed via the group's `members` property, which the template reads as `members`. (2) The finding's claim that the server previously returned everyone and now limits to non-automatic groups is not verifiable from current server code — GroupsController#members limits all groups uniformly; grade the observable defect (only 50 shown, no way to paginate), not the historical attribution. The cited line `model.findMembers()` itself is not wrong; the missing piece is pagination/all-members loading in the public view.

items.defectStatement: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, `group.users.delete(user_id)` removes the membership but never clears the user's `primary_group_id`. A user whose primary group was this group therefore keeps that group as their primary group (flair/title) after being removed, contradicting the intended behavior exercised in spec/models/user_spec.rb:1021-1027, where removing a user from a group unsets `primary_group_id`.
obligations: After a successful remove_member, the removed user's primary_group_id must be cleared (set to nil/NULL) when it equals the group's id.
The membership must actually be removed (the GroupUser row is gone / group.users no longer includes the user).
primary_group_id must NOT be cleared for a user whose primary group is a different group (the reset is conditional on primary_group_id == group.id).
Existing behavior must be preserved: automatic groups still respond 422 via can_not_modify_automatic, and a valid non-automatic removal still returns success_json.
items.notes: Any implementation that yields the above behavior is valid (e.g. `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)`, or delegating to group.remove plus a model-level reset). The finding slightly overstates the history: the old update_patch delete path used group.remove(user), which destroys GroupUser directly and also did not reset primary_group_id; the reset lived in Group#destroy_deletions, reached via the bulk `group.usernames=` path. Regardless, the non-member-keeps-flair outcome is the genuine defect. Be tolerant of nil/nonexistent user ids and note that the group.save after the update_all is not required for correctness.

items.defectStatement: The host format regex permits an optional `:port` and `before_validation` only strips the scheme and path, so a record can be stored as e.g. `example.com:8080`. But `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and matches only on `uri.host` (port dropped) with `lower(host) = ?`, so such records can never be found: `host_allowed?` returns false and embedding/retrieval is silently denied (and conversely a portless record matches any port). Port information in the stored host and the incoming URL is never reconciled.
obligations: A record stored with an explicit non-default port (e.g. 'example.com:8080') must be matched by an incoming URL that uses that same host and port.
Matching must still work for existing portless records with portless/default-port URLs (preserve current passing behavior: trims scheme and path; multiple hosts; non-matching host returns false).

Ports must be compared consistently so that a record with port A does not match a URL using a different explicit port B, and host-only/URL-only port combinations resolve to a single, well-defined rule (e.g. default ports 80/443 treated as absent).

Keep `record_for_host` returning the matching record (or false/nil) and `host_allowed?` returning a boolean; callers embed_controller's referer check, TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, and TopicEmbed must continue to work.
items.notes: Two valid fix families: (a) reject ports in the validation regex so stored hosts never contain one, or (b) keep ports and build the lookup key from `uri.host` plus `uri.port` when it differs from the URI scheme's default. The finding is accurate; note it cuts both ways — the current code also matches a portless record to a URL with an arbitrary explicit port, so a correct fix should decide default-port normalization. The unrelated lowercasing mismatch (column lowercased but the bound `host` parameter is not explicitly downcased) is outside this finding and need not be fixed, though it is acceptable if a fix touches it.

items.defectStatement: In CreateEmbeddableHosts#change, the results of the embed_category join query (line 11) and the uncategorized_category_id query (line 15) are dereferenced via [0]['id']/[0]['value'] without any nil check. When a setting row is absent (embed_category has no default in config/site_settings.yml, so the join returns no rows on upgrades that never set it; uncategorized_category_id can also be missing), execute(...)[0] is nil and the migration raises (NoMethodError/IndexError) instead of defaulting category_id, so the whole migration aborts.
obligations: Before reading ['id'] from the embed_category query result, guard for an empty/nil row and set category_id to 0 (not crash) when no matching category/setting exists, so the existing `if category_id == 0` fallback still runs.
Before reading ['value'] from the uncategorized_category_id query result, guard for an empty/nil row and fall back to a safe default (e.g. 0) rather than dereferencing nil.

Preserve existing resolution behavior when rows are present: category_id must be the category id whose name equals embed_category's value, or the uncategorized_category_id value when that lookup yields 0.
Leave the embeddable_hosts insertion loop (lines 18-29) and the final DELETE (line 31) semantics intact; the resolved category_id must still be used in the INSERT statements.
items.notes: The finding is accurate and the failure is on the normal upgrade path: embed_category has no entry in config/site_settings.yml, so the join query legitimately returns zero rows. Note the sibling migration db/migrate/20140715190552_remove_uncategorized_parents.rb uses the same execute(...)[0]['value'] pattern but guards it with `uncat && uncat[0] && uncat[0]['value']`, confirming execute(...)[0] can be nil in this codebase (so the error may present as NoMethodError, or IndexError on some adapters — either way it aborts). Guarding the second query is also warranted per that sibling migration's treatment of uncategorized_category_id, even though fixtures seed it. Any valid guard idiom is acceptable (nil checks, `.first`, SQL COALESCE/default in config); the SQL-injection risk from interpolating `h` at line 25 is a separate concern and out of scope for this finding.

items.defectStatement: In the save success callback (embeddable-host.js.es6:37-38), the component overwrites the saved record's category using the submitted component property `this.get('categoryId')` instead of the category the server actually stored. When a new host is saved with no category selected, `categoryId` is null, `Discourse.Category.findById(null)` returns undefined (category.js:241-244), so `host.category` is cleared and the row renders an empty category badge until reload, even though the server assigned `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` and returned it in the serializer payload.
obligations: After a successful save, host.category must reflect the category the server actually stored, including the blank/no-selection case where the server substitutes the uncategorized category, so the displayed category badge is not empty.
For a save where the user did select/change a category, the badge must still show that selected category (existing correct behavior preserved).
The success path must still reset editToggled to false and the failure path must still surface the error via popupAjaxError (or equivalent); no uncaught errors for a null/missing category id.
Resolving an id that has no matching category must not throw; findById already returns undefined for falsy ids and callers must tolerate that.
items.notes: Server side confirms the defect: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host sets category_id to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when blank and EmbeddableHostSerializer returns category_id. The rest adapter (rest.js.es6:56-72) returns the response payload, and Ember Data applies it to the record before save() resolves, so a fix can read the server value via host.get('category_id') after the promise resolves (or otherwise use the returned category_id). Reading categoryId only when it is non-null is an alternative but still misses the server-substituted uncategorized id. The finding is accurate; note categoryId is set from host.category.id in the edit action, so the bug specifically bites new hosts or any save with a blank chooser value, and it can leave host.category undefined for later edit attempts.

items.defectStatement: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, `i.content` comes from SimpleRSS, which only populates `content` for `content:encoded` or Atom `<content>` elements. For plain RSS 2.0 items that carry only `<description>`, `i.content` is nil, so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. Because the job is `retry: false` and `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` also invokes this job synchronously, one such item aborts the whole feed import and the fallback HTTP embed path for the requested URL.
obligations: When `i.content` is present, its scrubbed and CGI.unescapeHTML-decoded value must still be used as the body (existing clean-HTML behavior preserved).
When `i.content` is nil/blank but `i.description` is present, the description must be used as the body instead of raising.
Items for which both `content` and `description` are blank must be skipped (via `next`) so no empty topic is imported and no error is raised.

Existing per-item behavior must be preserved: the `i.link`/`i.id` URL fallback and the `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, body)` call with the resolved body, and no exception should abort processing of remaining items.
items.notes: TopicEmbed.import already returns nil for non-http(s) URLs and expects a mutable String (it does `contents << ...`), so the body passed must be a String, not nil. A valid alternative is `body = i.content.presence || i.description` then `next if body.blank?`; the exact form of the nil/blank guard is not important. Note the finding's claim that RSS `description` is a reliable fallback is correct for SimpleRSS (it exposes `description`), but do not change behavior for items that do have content. Title/URL handling is out of scope.

items.defectStatement: In EmbedController#best, an anonymous request for any embed_url that is not yet in TopicEmbed enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic with no rate limit on the enqueue itself (user_id is nil for anonymous users). The only throttle is inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? and is keyed on the exact embed_url string (redis key "retrieved:#{@embed_url}", 60s), so N distinct paths on the embeddable host each enqueue a job, and each so-far-unseen URL also runs a full synchronous feed poll (TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), which downloads/parses the RSS and imports every item) plus a remote HTTP fetch via TopicEmbed.import_remote. The practical risk is job/network fanout proportional to distinct unseen URLs, not literally unbounded for a single repeated URL (that is caught by the 60s per-URL key).
obligations: Enqueueing from the unauthenticated embed request path must be rate-limited per client (IP) and/or globally, so many distinct embed_url values (~one per path) cannot each spawn a RetrieveTopic job.
The RSS feed poll must run at most once per interval regardless of how many retrievals occur; it must not be invoked synchronously once per retrieval inside TopicRetriever.

Existing behavior must be preserved: a known embed_url still renders the topic view, an unknown one still enqueues retrieval and renders 'loading', the embeddable/referer host checks remain, and the per-URL 60s throttle plus staff no_throttle bypass in TopicRetriever continue to work.
The fix must not break TopicRetriever/RetrieveTopic semantics for valid requests (host validation via invalid_host?, TopicEmbed existence short-circuits, staff bypass).
items.notes: Finding is partly overstated: a throttle does exist (retrieved_recently?, 60s per exact URL, redis setnx), and invalid_host? restricts retrieval to the configured embeddable host, so it is not literally unbounded for one URL. The genuine defects are (a) no per-IP/global limit on the enqueue path, and (b) feed polling run once per retrieval rather than per interval. Valid alternative fixes: throttle the controller/job by IP or globally; debounce PollFeed using the existing "feed-modified:#{SHA1(url)}" key or the scheduled recurrence; enqueue PollFeed asynchronously instead of executing it inline; guard with a last-poll timestamp. A fix that only changes the redis throttle key or only rate-limits the exact URL does not satisfy the requirement.

items.defectStatement: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the relative-URL check `href.start_with?('/')` (line 64) also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png`, and the rewrite then prefixes the embed host, turning them into `http://embedhost/cdn.example.com/a.png`. The identical check for `img src` at line 70 has the same bug, so external images/links in imported posts are corrupted.
obligations: Protocol-relative values beginning with '//' (both `` and ``) must be left unchanged, since they are valid external references resolved against the page scheme.

Genuinely root-relative single-slash values must still be rewritten to `#{prefix}/...` exactly as before (e.g. `/hello` -> `http://eviltrout.com/hello`, `/images/wat.jpg` -> `http://eviltrout.com/images/wat.jpg`).
Absolute URLs (http://, https://, etc.) and blank/nil attribute values must continue to be left untouched.
The fix must be applied consistently to both the loop (lines 62-67) and the loop (lines 68-73); paths remain the same otherwise.
items.notes: Finding is accurate. Any check that excludes a leading '//' but still matches a single leading '/' is valid (e.g. `start_with?('/') && !start_with?('//')`, regex `=~ %r{\A/(?!/)}`, or URI-joining). Traps: `//` must not be treated as a root-relative '/'; stripping leading slashes via `sub(/^\/+/, '')` is fine only after the protocol-relative case is excluded. Existing spec expects `/hello` and `/images/wat.jpg` rewritten to the embed host, so do not change that behavior. Only two occurrences exist in the repo (lines 64, 70); callers are TopicEmbed.import (create and revise paths).

items.defectStatement: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-42), when feed polling is enabled the code calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, which unconditionally imports every entry in the RSS/Atom feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-37, each `TopicEmbed.import` doing DB lookups and possibly topic/post creation). A single embed request for an unknown URL therefore performs O(N) heavy write operations over the whole feed before the `TopicEmbed.exists?` check, even when the target item was the first entry.
obligations: The targeted call must stop importing feed items once the requested embed_url has been imported (early exit / item filtering), so a feed of N items no longer causes N imports per embed request for a URL that appears early or is already present.

`perform_retrieve` must still invoke the feed-polling path when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, and must still fall through to `fetch_http` when the embed is not found after polling (i.e. preserve the `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` short-circuit).

The scheduled hourly `Jobs::PollFeed` job invoked with no/empty args must keep importing the entire feed unchanged; any early-exit or URL filtering must be opt-in so the periodic job is not restricted to a single item.
The target URL must be communicated to the job (e.g. via `execute` args) since `poll_feed` does not have access to `@embed_url`.
items.notes: The finding's suggested `break` on `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` inside `poll_feed` is not directly implementable in poll_feed.rb since `@embed_url` belongs to TopicRetriever; the URL must be passed through job args (or the filtering done another way). Valid fixes include: passing `embed_url: @embed_url` in the `execute` call and having `poll_feed` skip/stop once that embed exists, or adding a targeted single-item import path. Preserving the no-args scheduled behavior is the key regression trap. Note the DIFF only adds this new file; the finding correctly characterizes the code as shown.

items.defectStatement: In TopicEmbed.import, the untrusted `url` is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted `href` attribute and into the link text of an HTML string that is stored as the post body and cooked with `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (Post#cook returns `raw` verbatim), so a URL containing `'`/`<`/`>` can break out of the anchor and inject arbitrary markup/attributes into the rendered post. The `url` reaches this line from the `embed_url` request parameter (EmbedController#best → retrieve_topic → TopicRetriever, which only checks URI host) and directly from RSS feed item links in Jobs::PollFeed, so it is attacker-influenceable.
obligations: The URL inserted into the `<a href='...'>` attribute and into the link text must be HTML-escaped so characters like `'`, `"`, `<`, `>` and `&` in the URL cannot terminate the attribute or start new tags/attributes.
The anchor markup itself (`...`) must remain real HTML that is passed to the I18n `embed.imported_from` (`%{link}`) key; escaping must be applied to the URL value, not to the entire link string.
For ordinary/well-formed URLs (e.g. http://eviltrout.com/123) the produced link text and href are unchanged, and the post is still created/updated and cooked as raw_html exactly as before.
The surrounding `<hr><small>...</small>` wrapper and the I18n translation lookup are preserved.
items.notes: Valid fixes include ERB::Util.html_escape(url) (or `h`) applied to both interpolations, or building the anchor with Nokogiri (set href and text; Nokogiri escapes on serialization). Do not escape the whole `<a ...>` string, or the link renders as literal text. The downstream absolutize_urls re-parses the content with Nokogiri, which also encodes stray quote characters, but escaping at this line is the expected fix and is checked directly. Finding is essentially accurate; minor nuance: TopicRetriever does compare the host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but only the host is checked (path/query are free), and the PollFeed path performs no host check at all — in both cases the full URL is untrusted. User-visible URL text should still display the original URL characters (escaped entities decode back in the browser).

items.defectStatement: TopicEmbed.import_remote (line 48) fetches the caller-supplied `url` with Kernel#open (open-uri) with no restriction on scheme, port, redirect target or timeout. The only upstream guard, TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, compares URI(url).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host, so it constrains the *host* but not the port, scheme, path or redirects; open-uri follows HTTP redirects, so a redirect issued by the (attacker-reachable) embeddable host to an internal/link-local address is fetched server-side, and the disqus.thor caller invokes import_remote directly with no validation at all.
obligations: The fetch at line 48 must not be able to retrieve non-HTTP(S) URLs or be reinterpreted as a local file/pipe/subprocess (e.g. a leading '|' or file:// URL) by Kernel#open.
Redirects must be either disabled or re-validated: a redirect from the allowed host to a private, loopback, link-local, or otherwise internal address must not be followed and read.

Legitimate behavior must be preserved: for a normal http/https embed URL whose content is a readable HTML page, the fetched body is still passed to Readability::Document.new with the same tags/attributes options, and import_remote still delegates to TopicEmbed.import with the title/content.
The fetch must be bounded (a read/open timeout or equivalent) so it cannot hang indefinitely.
items.notes: The finding overstates the direct example: because invalid_host? requires URI(url).host == embeddable_host, `http://eviltrout.com:6379/...` connects to the embeddable host on port 6379, not to an arbitrary internal host — the real SSRF vector is the unvalidated scheme/port plus open-uri's default redirect-following (and no timeout), and any fix that only adds a host check is insufficient. Note lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 calls import_remote directly (bypassing invalid_host? entirely) and lib/oneboxer.rb:61 / other oneboxer files use the same `open(url).read` pattern, so a shared/hardened fetcher is a valid alternative fix; grading should accept any change at line 48 (or a helper it calls) that satisfies the obligations, not one specific implementation.

items.defectStatement: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss line 497, the light-theme color for `.group-member-info .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` inside the new `dark-light-choose(...)` wrapper. Because `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument in the light theme (brightness($primary) < brightness($secondary)), this changes the light-theme rendering of the name, not just adds dark-theme support.
obligations: The light-theme result for `.group-member-info .name` must revert to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, matching the pre-change value.

The dark-theme branch must still be provided (dark-light-choose wrapper retained) so the element is legible under the dark theme; the value should match the established convention `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` used for equivalent `.name` styles (common/base/user.scss:124) and neighboring dark-theme text (mobile/modal.scss:102).
All other declarations of `.group-member-info .name` (`display: inline-block; margin-top: 5px; vertical-align: inherit;`) must remain unchanged.
The unrelated `.title` (line 503) and `.fa/.icon` (line 489) rules must not be altered, since they correctly use 50% lightness in both themes.
items.notes: Finding is accurate; diff confirms light-theme lightness was 30% before. Note the fix necessarily also introduces dark-theme handling (the original had no `dark-light-choose`), so a valid fix must preserve/add a dark-theme value in addition to restoring 30% for light. Using 70% for the dark branch is the repo convention but any legible dark value that preserves dark-theme intent is acceptable as long as the light-theme 30% is restored. Do not touch `.title`; its 50%/50% is intentional per common/base/user.scss:129.

items.defectStatement: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss line 102, the .custom-message-length color passes darkness/lightness values in the wrong order to dark-light-choose: the light-theme result uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and the dark-theme result uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%). This inverts the original light appearance (the old rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)) and contradicts the matching desktop/modal.scss rule, which uses (70%, 30%).
obligations: The light-theme result must be scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) (matching desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length).
The dark-theme result must be scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) (matching desktop/modal.scss .custom-message-length).
The arguments must be ordered correctly for dark-light-choose, whose first argument is the light-theme result and second is the dark-theme result (see common/foundation/variables.scss).
Preserve the rest of the .custom-message-length rule unchanged (selector, margin, font-size) and keep the property applying only to that selector.
items.notes: dark-light-choose($light-theme-result, $dark-theme-result) selects on brightness($primary) < brightness($secondary). The desktop rule at desktop/modal.scss lines 50 and 94 both use exactly (70%, 30%), which is the intended pairing. A fix that only reverts to the pre-change scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) would restore light behavior but drop the dark-theme handling the change was adding, so the stated two-theme form is preferred; the grader should accept any form producing 70%/$primary for light and 30%/$secondary for dark. Only line 102 is in scope; the other (30%, 70%) occurrences in common/base/topic-post.scss and common/base/user.scss are different rules and not part of this finding.

items.defectStatement: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss line 522, `.group-member-info .name` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme branch (chosen when `$primary` is darker than `$secondary`, i.e. the normal light theme) now renders a medium primary instead of the original dark primary, regressing the username color's contrast.
obligations: The light-theme argument for `.group-member-info .name` in desktop/user.scss must be restored to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; it must not remain 50%.
The rule must keep using `dark-light-choose(...)` with two theme arguments so the dark theme gets an appropriate (light) color rather than the light-theme value.
The dark-theme argument should be `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`, matching the convention already used for user names in common/base/user.scss (lines 119/124).
The existing declarations in the `.name` block (`display: inline-block;`, `margin-top: 5px;`) and the sibling `.title` rule (line 527, which legitimately uses 50%/50%) must be preserved/unchanged.
items.notes: The finding is accurate; the diff confirms the original single-arg value was 30%. The cited line (522) is the only line in scope. Alternative fix worth accepting: any equivalent expression producing the same colors per theme (e.g. inlining the values) is behaviorally fine. Trap: `mobile/user.scss` line 497 has an identical `.name` selector still using 50%/50%, and the sibling `.title` uses 50%/50% matching common/base/user.scss `.title`; do not let those distract from the `.name` regression. The 70% dark-theme value is backed by common/base/user.scss `.name`/`.username a` (30%/70%) and is what the finding requests.

items.defectStatement: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the equal-length branch (lines 144–146) decides that two hosts share a parent domain by stripping only their first label and comparing the remainder. For hosts under a multi-label public suffix this matches unrelated sites: `forum.co.uk` and `evil.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`, so an external site is treated as being on the forum's domain and its full URL path is appended (e.g. `evil.co.uk/user`), even though the feature should show the path only for sites on the forum's own registrable domain.
obligations: Two hosts must be treated as the same domain only when they share the same registrable domain (eTLD+1); specifically `forum.co.uk` vs `evil.co.uk` must not match, and the result for `evil.co.uk` (with some path) must be just `evil.co.uk` with no path appended.

Preserve existing correct behavior: identical hosts return host + path (`example.com` == `example.com` -> `example.com/user`); `www.example.com` vs discourse host `forum.example.com` still match and return host + path; and website `example.com` with discourse host `forums.example.com` still returns `example.com/user`.
Unrelated hosts continue to return only the host with no path (e.g. website `example.com`, discourse host `discourse.org` -> `example.com`).
Nil/blank handling is preserved: when `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil the method still returns nil and `include_website_name` behavior is unchanged.
items.notes: The public_suffix gem is NOT currently a repo dependency (no references anywhere), so a fix cannot simply require it without adding a dependency; any label-based or curated multi-part-suffix comparison that yields the correct registrable domain is acceptable. The cited branch is not exercised by existing specs (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb only covers the first `if` and the `else` branches), so tests may need adding. The finding's alternative suggestion 'requiring at least three labels after removing the subdomain' is imprecise: taken literally it would also reject the valid `www.example.com`/`forum.example.com` case (parent `example.com` has only two labels) — the grader should accept any solution that correctly compares registrable domains, not that exact phrasing. The first `if` and the `else` branch (line 149, parent-domain check via `ends_with?("." << website_host)`) are correct and should not be broken.

items.defectStatement: `include_website_name` (user_serializer.rb:153) is missing the trailing `?` that every other AMS include guard in this file uses, so ActiveModel::Serializers never recognizes it as an include guard and treats `website_name` as always-included. Because `:website_name` is not in the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), the website host/path derived from the hidden `website` attribute is still serialized for users where `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. TL0 users viewed by anonymous visitors).
obligations: When `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (TL0 user + anonymous scope), `website_name` must not appear in the serialized JSON, matching how `website` itself is hidden.
When the user is not restricted and has a website, `website_name` must still be serialized with the existing value (same host/path computation as the current `website_name` method).

The include guard must actually be honored by AMS (name ending in `?`, or generated via `untrusted_attributes`), and it must not regress the `website.present?` behavior: no non-nil website_name value when website is blank/absent.
The `website_name` value computation (lines 137-151) must remain unchanged.
items.notes: Finding is accurate. Two valid fixes: (a) rename to `include_website_name?` returning `website.present? && !scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`; (b) add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), whose helper defines `include_website_name?` as `false if scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` else `website_name.present?` (remove/replace the broken method). Trap: merely renaming to `include_website_name?` while keeping only `website.present?` does NOT fix the leak, because with no restriction the attribute is still emitted for restricted users. Note `website_name` was added to the `attributes` declaration (line 43), not to untrusted_attributes, so the finding's second clause is correct. Existing specs (spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:76-90) use a default Fabricate(:user) with TrustLevel[1], so they remain non-restricted and expect `website_name` present; the TL0-anonymous context's `untrusted_attributes` list (spec line 11) would ideally gain `:website_name`, but that is a test-only change.

items.defectStatement: In `UserSerializer#website_name` (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:147-150), the same-domain fallback only checks `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, i.e. it matches only when the instance host is a subdomain of the website host. When the relationship is reversed — the user's website host is a subdomain of the instance host (e.g. website `http://forum.example.com/user`, instance `example.com`) — the label counts differ so the branch at line 144 is skipped, and line 149 is also false; the method returns the bare host and silently drops the distinguishing URL path. The check needs to match in both directions (or the reverse direction as well) before returning the bare host.
obligations: When the user's website host is a subdomain of the Discourse instance host (e.g. website 'http://forum.example.com/user' with instance host 'example.com'), website_name must include the URL path (e.g. 'forum.example.com/user'), not just the bare host.

Existing behavior must be preserved: equal hosts return host+path ('example.com' == 'example.com' -> 'example.com/user'); a website host that is the parent of the instance host returns host+path (website 'example.com' with instance 'forums.example.com' -> 'example.com/user'); two same-length (>2 labels) hosts sharing the same suffix after the first label return host+path; and unrelated hosts return the bare host (website 'example.com' with instance 'discourse.org' -> 'example.com').

The added subdomain match must respect a label/dot boundary (equivalently test the suffix after a leading '.'), so hosts that merely share a string suffix without a label boundary (e.g. 'myexample.com' vs 'example.com') are not treated as the same site and still return the bare host.
When the website is blank/unparseable so no host can be extracted, website_name must still return nil (unchanged).
items.notes: The finding's WHY text slightly misquotes line 149 as `discourse_host.ends_with?(website_host)`; the code actually concatenates a leading dot (`"." << website_host`). The directional conclusion is still correct, and the dot boundary must be kept in any reverse-direction check. The cited code is the real branch structure (exact match / equal-length same-suffix / ends_with); a valid fix can add a symmetric reverse check, restructure into a shared same-site helper, or treat parent and subdomain cases uniformly — all are acceptable as long as the listed behaviors hold. Note the reverse case cannot fall into the line-144 branch because the label counts differ, so it genuinely relies on the fallback branch.

items.defectStatement: In `validateUploadedFile` (utilities.js lines 180-186) the client-side upload size limit is hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB instead of reading the configured value `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. As a result the client ignores admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`: it rejects files that are within a configured limit and, for other files, shows a max-size message that does not match the enforced limit. The existing test "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" (max_image_size_kb=5, 10KB file) now fails because 10KB is not > 10240KB.
obligations: The comparison limit is derived from the client site settings for the given upload type: 'image' -> Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb, 'attachment' -> Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb (equivalently the dynamic `['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup).
Comparison must remain in KB units: fileSizeKB = file.size / 1024 compared against the setting value (which is expressed in kB), preserving the existing 10KB-with-5KB-limit rejection.
The bootbox alert for post.errors.file_too_large must report the same configured limit that was enforced via max_size_kb, not a hardcoded 10MB value.
The rest of validateUploadedFile must be preserved: authorized-extension check, new-user restriction/type-specific alert, and the true return when all checks pass.
items.notes: The correct value is already client-exposed: site_settings.yml marks max_image_size_kb (default 3072) and max_attachment_size_kb (default 3072) as client:true. The defect is not overstated. Note the same hunk of the same change also hardcodes 10*1024 in displayErrorForUpload's 413 branch (line 246, which originally used max_image_size_kb); that second line is outside the cited 180-186 range but is the same class of regression and may be addressed by a broader fix. The finding's claim about capping image uploads assumes an admin sets max_image_size_kb above 10MB; that is valid but secondary to matching the configured limit.

items.defectStatement: In create_upload, each downsize attempt calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) with the same source and destination path while the Tempfile object is still open, so the loop guard `tempfile.size` and the later reads of `tempfile` (FastImage, Digest::SHA1.file) are sized/read through the already-open file descriptor. If ImageMagick replaces the file with a new inode, the descriptor keeps pointing at the original large file, so the guard never sees the reduced size (it runs all 5 attempts) and Upload.create_for receives a stale size and content rather than the downsampled file.
obligations: After each downsize, the size compared by the while-loop guard against SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes must reflect the file actually on disk, so the loop terminates once the image is within the limit (or after 5 attempts).

The file/IO handed to Upload.create_for must read the downsampled bytes, not the stale original: the size argument, the bytes FastImage reads, and the sha1 Digest::SHA1.file computes must all come from the downsized content, and the IO must be rewound as needed before it is reused.

Preserve the existing guards and limits: no downsizing when tempfile is nil, tempfile.size is 0, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb <= 0, or the filename is not an image; keep the 5-attempt cap and pass allow_animation from SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails.
The ensure block must still close/delete the original Tempfile (tempfile.try(:close!)) and any intermediate downsize temp file must not be leaked.
items.notes: The finding is directionally correct that sizing/reads must be path-based or the Tempfile reopened, but its stated consequence is partly overstated: Upload.create_for stores the file with File.open(file.path) (upload.rb:138), so the stored bytes can still be the downsized ones; the concrete symptoms are a guard that never sees the new size (running all 5 attempts) and a mismatched sha1/filesize (stale FD read) versus stored content. Whether an in-place convert actually changes the inode is ImageMagick-version dependent, so a fix should not rely on the open FD staying valid. Valid fixes include: downsample to a separate temp path then FileUtils.mv over the original and reopen/rewind the Tempfile, or drop the Tempfile FD and use File.size(tempfile.path) plus File.open(path) when passing to Upload.create_for. Note the same in-place resize pattern exists at upload.rb:98 (OptimizedImage.resize(file.path, file.path, ...)) but that is out of scope for this finding.

items.defectStatement: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic (common for users who received a topic email but never opened the topic). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError and breaking the unsubscribe link.
obligations: unsubscribe must not raise when no TopicUser row exists for the current user and topic; a row must be created (with the correct user_id and topic_id) and persisted so the unsubscribe takes effect.
Existing behavior must be preserved: when a row's notification_level is greater than :regular it is set to :regular, otherwise (including :regular, :muted, or no existing row) it is set to :muted.
The resulting change must be saved (the controller must not silently skip persistence), and the action must still complete with perform_show_response as before.
items.notes: TopicUser.get(topic_id, user_id) only replaces find_by and still returns nil, so the suggested 'use TopicUser.get' alone is NOT a fix unless paired with handling/creating the missing record (e.g. `tu ||= TopicUser.new(...)` or TopicUser.change). When creating a row for the unsubscribe case, the correct outcome is notification_level = :muted (the else branch), so a fix that defaults new rows to muted is valid; a fix that reaches the :regular branch for a new row would be wrong. TopicUser.change(user_id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) is another valid approach since it creates-or-updates and sets notifications_changed_at/reason_id. Note current_user may also be nil if the route is hit without a session; a robust fix should not dereference nil for that case either.

items.defectStatement: The client-side topic-unsubscribe route's model hook loads the topic by calling PostStream.loadTopicView(id), which only issues a GET to the normal topic JSON endpoint (/t/:id.json). It never invokes the unsubscribe action, so a client-side transition into this route renders the "notifications stopped" message while the user's notification level for the topic is unchanged. Only a full server page load of /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe (TopicsController#unsubscribe) actually changes the level.
obligations: Entering the route via a client-side transition must actually change the topic's notification level server-side (equivalent to TopicsController#unsubscribe): drop to :regular when the current level is above regular (tracking/watching) and to :muted otherwise.
The unsubscribe/preference-changing request must complete successfully before the route shows the unsubscribe confirmation; the UI must not claim success while the level is unchanged.

The route must still load the topic data needed by the template/view (topic id, fancyTitle for the stop_notifications text, details.notification_level for topic-notifications-button) so the page renders as before.
Existing route behavior must be preserved: afterModel clearing details.notificationReasonText and didTransition setting application showFooter to true.
items.notes: An acceptable alternative fix is to not auto-unsubscribe in the model hook but make the page require an explicit submission (e.g., the notification button / a confirm button) that performs the level change. Server logic to mirror: TopicsController#unsubscribe sets notification_level to regular if it was > regular, else to muted, then saves. loadTopicView resolves /t/:id.json (confirmed in post-stream.js.es6), so it cannot trigger the unsubscribe action; the response for unsubscribe uses perform_show_response. The finding is accurate; the template text promising notifications are stopped is what makes the missing request user-visible.

items.defectStatement: The new `unsubscribe` action mutates persistent state (setting the current user's `TopicUser#notification_level` and calling `save!`) and it is reachable via a plain GET: `config/routes.rb` registers `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, and `ApplicationController`'s `protect_from_forgery` only verifies the CSRF token on non-GET requests. Because the action was also added to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, any third-party page can embed a link or `` and silently change a logged-in victim's notification level for that topic. The finding is accurate; the only "confirmation" is the client-side Ember unsubscribe template, which a direct GET bypasses entirely.
obligations: A state-changing request that a third-party origin can initiate without the user's participation (a bare cross-site GET, link, or image) must not change the user's notification level. The endpoint must either verify CSRF authenticity on a non-GET method or require a per-user credential (e.g. a signed token) that an attacker cannot forge.

The legitimate flow must still work: an authenticated user who follows the unsubscribe URL from the email/UI must still have the topic notification level raised to `regular` when it is currently above `regular`, and otherwise set to `muted`.

Existing routing/format behavior must be preserved: when the slug does not match, or the request is not JSON and the slug is blank, the action must still redirect (301) to the topic's `unsubscribe_url` instead of mutating.

Any change to the HTTP method, route, or added token must keep all callers working — the notification email link built from `topic.unsubscribe_url` (used in app/mailers/user_notifications.rb) and the client-side route `topicUnsubscribe` in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/app-route-map.js.es6 — so email unsubscribe links are not broken.
items.notes: Routes are GET (config/routes.rb:440-441); Rails' `protect_from_forgery` in ApplicationController only covers non-GET, so a GET that writes is inherently CSRF-able — this is the core defect. Both suggested remedies are valid: (a) require POST/PUT with CSRF token, or (b) require a signed per-user token in the URL (analogous to the existing `email_unsubscribe`/`key` flow). Note that a pure POST change is awkward because links in email cannot POST, so a token/confirmation approach is the more likely accepted fix; the Ember unsubscribe page already renders a notification control but that is client-side only and does not protect the server action. Also, `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: ..., topic_id: ...)` can return nil, so `tu.notification_level`/`tu.save!` can raise NoMethodError — a pre-existing bug outside this finding, but a fix should not rely on `tu` being non-nil without handling the nil case. `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` is what allows non-XHR navigation/image requests to reach the action; be aware whether the fix keeps or narrows it.

items.defectStatement: The new fallback chain in config/initializers/i18n.rb makes the result of a translation depend on SiteSetting.default_locale (the middle entry of the fallback list), but the translate_accelerator LRU cache key in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72 is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". For a logged-in user whose I18n.locale differs from the site default and whose string is resolved through the fallback, the resolved value is cached under key+user-locale without the default locale, so after an admin changes SiteSetting.default_locale the user keeps receiving the old default-locale text until cache eviction/restart.
obligations: After SiteSetting.default_locale changes, translations for a user whose locale differs from the default must reflect the new default locale, not the previously cached fallback value: either the default locale must be part of the cache key used by I18n.translate, or the I18n LRU cache (@cache) must be cleared/invalidated when default_locale changes.

The fallback resolution order and semantics must be preserved: [I18n.locale/user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en], de-duplicated and with nil/non-symbol entries removed (the .uniq.compact behavior).

FallbackLocaleList must keep responding to [] and ensure_loaded! (used by I18n.fallbacks and application_controller#set_locale) so that each fallback locale, including the current default locale, is still loaded on demand.
The fix must not disable the LRU translation caching for existing (non-fallback) lookups or change results for locales/keys that do not depend on the default-locale fallback.
items.notes: The finding is accurate but its cited line (i18n.rb:17) is only where SiteSetting.default_locale enters the lookup; the actual stale-cache logic lives in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72. A fix that only edits line 17 cannot by itself change the cache key, so accept any fix that meets the obligations, e.g. adding SiteSetting.default_locale to the LRU cache key in translate_accelerator.rb, or clearing I18n's @cache (I18n.reload! nils @cache / @loaded_locales) when the setting changes. Note nuances: (a) for anonymous users I18n.locale is set to SiteSetting.default_locale (application_controller#set_locale:152-157), so their key already changes and the bug mainly affects logged-in users with current_user.effective_locale != default; (b) ensure_loaded! (application_controller:159) only loads locales and does not clear the cache; (c) the default_locale setting has refresh: true, but nothing wires it to the I18n cache; (d) a fix must keep :en and dedup/compact behavior; (e) adding the setting to the key makes the existing cache entries in the same process unreachable but does not require reloading locales.

items.defectStatement: The added call `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` only force-loads the fallback locales on the web-request path (ApplicationController#set_locale), but Discourse's on-demand loader (I18n.load_locale/translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb) only loads `config.locale`. Any I18n.t outside a request — Jobs::Base (`I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`) and PostAlerter (`I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)`) — therefore never loads the other locales in the fallback chain, so lookup misses in the active locale return missing-text instead of falling back to default_locale/:en. The fallbacks backend is installed globally, so this affects every translate, not just requests.
obligations: After the fix, I18n.t calls made outside ApplicationController#set_locale (e.g. Jobs::Base's `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` path and PostAlerter's `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)` block) must resolve keys through the configured fallback chain [locale, default_locale, :en] when the active locale lacks the key, instead of returning 'translation missing'.

Loading must stay lazy/on-demand: only the locales needed for the current fallback chain may be loaded; do not eagerly load every supported locale, and do not regress the existing request-path behavior for current_user.effective_locale / SiteSetting.default_locale.

Fallback ordering and locale selection must be preserved: the list is still [I18n.locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en] with duplicates/compacts handled, and I18n.locale is applied before the chain is loaded.

Any loader change must remain safe for concurrent use (the load is guarded by LOAD_MUTEX / @loaded_locales) and must not drop/duplicate already-loaded locales or break the translation cache keyed on config.locale.
items.notes: Root cause is in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb: `translate`/`load_locale` load only `config.locale`, so fallbacks silently fail everywhere the request before_filter didn't run. The robust fix belongs there (e.g. have translate/load_locale load every locale in I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]) or at each non-request entry point (jobs/mailers); a change confined to application_controller.rb line 159 cannot fix jobs/mailers and would most likely be a removal of the now-redundant line. Allow either approach. Traps: (a) `PostAlerter` uses I18n.with_locale, which restores I18n.locale after the block, so any stateful preloading must be per-locale, not global; (b) the translation cache key includes config.locale, so distinct fallback locales must not collide; (c) the finding's mention of 'mailers' is indirect (mailers are sent via Jobs), and the concrete non-request call sites verified are app/jobs/base.rb:151 and app/services/post_alerter.rb:138.

items.defectStatement: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 70), hasPermission is called with both AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW and AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, and hasPermission returns true if any of the passed scopes is granted. As a result canManage() is identical to canView(): a subject holding only the all-groups VIEW permission is treated as able to manage all groups, so manage-only endpoints such as GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (auth.groups().requireManage()) and GroupResource manage endpoints let a read-only group viewer create/update/delete groups. The sibling canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) and UserPermissionsV2.canManage use MANAGE only, confirming this is an unintended copy of canView.
obligations: canManage() must return true only when the subject is actually authorized to MANAGE groups (or holds the MANAGE_USERS realm admin role), and must return false when the subject has only the all-groups VIEW permission.
The no-arg canManage() must no longer pass AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW to hasPermission; only MANAGE (and any other genuinely manage-equivalent scope) may be accepted.
The MANAGE_USERS admin-role short-circuit and the hasPermission all-groups evaluation path for users who genuinely have MANAGE must still work.
canView() and canView(GroupModel) behavior must remain unchanged (still accept VIEW or MANAGE).
items.notes: requireManage() is not overridden in GroupPermissionsV2; it is inherited from GroupPermissions and calls the overridden canManage(), so fixing line 70 fixes the callers automatically. Callers confirmed: GroupsResource.java:181 (addTopLevelGroup/create top-level group), GroupResource.java:120/158/197/270/356. A fix may equivalently delegate to super.canManage() (as ClientPermissionsV2 does) so long as VIEW alone no longer grants manage. The finding is accurate; no overstatement.

items.defectStatement: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() (lines 121-125), the callback uses groupResource.getId() (the authorization Resource UUID) both as the argument to hasPermission(...) and as the value added to the returned set. Group resources are created with the group id as their name: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(...GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, id) sets name = resolveGroup(...), which returns group.getId(), and hasPermission(groupId,...) resolves the resource via resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Passing the resource UUID therefore fails the per-group lookup and falls back to the all-groups resource, and the set returned to callers contains resource UUIDs instead of group ids, so UserModel.GROUPS filtering (UsersResource.searchForUser) matches no users.
obligations: The returned Set<String> must contain group ids (the group resource's name, which equals the group id), not resource UUIDs.

The per-group permission check must target the group resource by its group id / name so that per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are honored; it must not silently fall back to the all-groups resource because of an unresolvable identifier.
The existing early-return semantics must be preserved: empty set when root.users().canView(), when !root.isAdminSameRealm(), or when the resource server is null.
The same identifier must be used consistently for the permission evaluation and for the value added to the granted set.
items.notes: A valid fix is to replace both groupResource.getId() occurrences with groupResource.getName() (the resource name equals the group id per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup). The finding is accurate; AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup(session, id) returns group.getId(), so resource name == group id. Equivalent to V1 GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), which also uses resource.getName() (there stripped of a prefix). Downstream use: UsersResource passes the set to session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) / getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds), which require real group ids. No null/edge concerns beyond the preserved early returns.

items.defectStatement: getSubGroups (services/.../admin/GroupResource.java:176-180) no longer evaluates the caller's global-view permission once; the diff replaced `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))` with `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)`, so every returned subgroup is passed through canView(GroupModel) individually. For a non-admin grantee whose view permission comes from an all-groups (V2) permission, each call performs a per-group resource lookup plus evaluatePermission, turning one global evaluation into N evaluations per page of subgroups.
obligations: getSubGroups must evaluate the global view permission (auth.groups().canView()) at most once per request, before filtering the subgroup stream.
When that global check is true, subgroups must not be individually re-checked with canView(group) (the fast path must short-circuit).
When the global check is false, filtering must still keep the per-subgroup auth.groups().canView(g) check, so an unauthorized subgroup is never returned.
The existing guard this.auth.groups().requireView(group) and the paginatedStream(...).map(...populateSubGroupCount/toRepresentation...) behavior must be preserved unchanged.
items.notes: The fix is behavior-preserving: in both implementations canView() == true implies canView(group) == true (GroupPermissions.canView(group) delegates to canView()/canManage(); GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) has the same MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS role check, and a global VIEW/MANAGE on the groups resource type satisfies the per-group evaluation). Valid alternatives: hoist `boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView();` and use `.filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`, or otherwise cache the global result once. Do not just drop the filter, and do not replace with getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (it changes semantics to view-members). Minor overstatement in the finding: for admin-role global viewers canView(group) early-returns after a role check, so the expensive N resource-lookups + evaluatePermission occur mainly for V2 all-groups grantees without the admin role; it is still N per-subgroup calls versus one. The unrelated second diff hunk (GroupModel child = null removed) is not part of this defect.

items.defectStatement: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (line 127) the granted group IDs are produced for the V2 admin-permissions schema, where group authorization resources are named with the bare group ID (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()); but the JPA consumer that receives this set, JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery (line 1081), still requires a resource named "group.resource."+groupId via LIKE. For V2-only group permissions no such prefixed resource exists, so the EXISTS predicate fails and UsersResource search/count paths return/count zero members of those groups despite the correct group IDs. (The same method also adds groupResource.getId(), which is a generated resource row id, not necessarily the group id the membership predicate compares against.)
obligations: For a realm using the V2 admin-permissions schema, a user who is a member of a group that has VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS granted must be included by the JPA search/count filtering driven by getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, and getUsersCount must equal the number of users returned by the corresponding search.

The set consumed by the JPA group-permission filtering must contain actual group IDs (values that match UserGroupMembership.groupId), not opaque authorization-resource row IDs; the group IDs returned here must be usable both for the membership predicate and for locating the corresponding V2 resource (name == group id).

Legacy/V1 behavior must be preserved: existing realms and migrated data with resources named "group.resource."+groupId must still filter members correctly, and getUserCount/search behavior for V1 must not regress.

The empty-set / null semantics of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission must be preserved for its existing callers (UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource), i.e. a caller that passes the set into the JPA filter must still get the same view-all vs no-permission behavior as before.
items.notes: Verified against the repo: AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() (so V2 group resources are named by bare group id, no prefix), JPAResourceStore.create with a 3-arg call generates a random id, and JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery uses LIKE "group.resource."||groupId — so the V1/V2 naming mismatch and broken filtering are real. The finding's requested fix location is the JPA filtering contract (JpaUserProvider), not the single cited line in GroupPermissionsV2; the cited line is the producer of the set. A fix that only changes line 127 to prefix names with "group.resource." would not work, because the same set is also matched against UserGroupMembership.groupId (bare group id), so a schema-aware branch in the JPA subquery (and returning bare group ids here) is the more plausible correct fix. Traps: line 123 adds resource.getId() rather than the group id/name, which may themselves not be group ids; also getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns an empty set both for "view all users" and for "no realm/schema", so any fix must not change those empty-set call sites' meaning. Verify the exact empty-vs-null handling in UsersResource/JpaUserProvider before finalizing.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String) (line 215-221), when the per-client resource is not found the fallback calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null (it returns null when the schema is unsupported, the resource type is unknown, or the "all-clients" resource is absent). The code then passes that potentially-null resource to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource), which dereferences resource.getId() and throws a NullPointerException instead of denying permission. The sibling hasPermission(String) overload (lines 244-247) correctly returns false when its resource lookup yields null.
obligations: After the fallback getResourceTypeResource call, if the returned resource is null the method must return false rather than call findByResource with null; no NullPointerException may be thrown in that case.

The normal path (per-client resource found) must be unchanged: null result of findByName still triggers the all-clients fallback, and when the all-clients resource exists evaluation proceeds as before.

Existing return semantics are preserved: false is returned when the caller is not an admin of the same realm, when the resource server is null, when no all-clients policies exist, and when no matching scope is granted.
The fix must keep the method's boolean return contract and not alter behavior for callers (canView/canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles).
items.notes: The finding is accurate and confirmed: getResourceTypeResource returns null in several cases (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:116-134), and JPAPolicyStore.findByResource dereferences resource.getId() (JPAPolicyStore.java:215). Adding `if (resource == null) return false;` immediately after the fallback assignment is the minimal correct fix; an equivalent is to null-check before the findByResource call. Note: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission(UserModel, EvaluationContext, String...) (UserPermissionsV2.java:119-126) has the identical defect with policyStore.findByResource(server, resource); fixing only the cited method leaves that sibling broken, but the graded replacement covers only the cited lines. Also note the evaluation block below (line 224) also dereferences resource, so a fix that only guards the findByResource call without returning false would still NPE; the requirement is to return false when the fallback resource is null.

items.defectStatement: In ClientPermissionsV2.canView() (lines 85-88), the check is canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW); it omits the fine-grained MANAGE permission on the all-clients resource that canManage() honors (line 73: super.canManage() || hasPermission(MANAGE)). A caller with only MANAGE on all clients therefore gets canManage()==true but canView()==false, so canList() (base ClientPermissions line 243: canView() || QUERY_* roles) and canViewClientScopes() also return false, denying list/view-all despite manage rights — inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel) (lines 118-122, VIEW||MANAGE) and with V1 where MANAGE_CLIENTS implies view.
obligations: canView() must return true for a caller that has the fine-grained MANAGE permission on the all-clients resource (i.e. hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), not just VIEW.

All existing true paths must be preserved: MANAGE_CLIENTS and VIEW_CLIENTS admin roles (canViewClientDefault()) and the fine-grained VIEW permission; callers with none of these must still return false.

As a consequence canList()/canListClientScopes() (which derive from canView() plus QUERY_* roles) and requireList() must now permit a MANAGE-only caller, matching canView(ClientScopeModel)'s VIEW||MANAGE semantics.
The change must be safe when there is no same-realm admin or no resource server: hasPermission(String) already guards these cases, so canView() must not throw.
isPermissionsEnabled / other unrelated methods must remain unaffected (no broad change to the V2 class beyond the view check).
items.notes: Two valid fix shapes: (a) append `|| hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` to canView(); (b) combine the existing checks with canManage(), e.g. `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)`. The finding's parenthetical "or delegate to canManage()" is only correct if combined with the VIEW_CLIENTS role and VIEW permission checks — replacing the body with canManage() alone would regress a VIEW_CLIENTS-only or VIEW-permission-only caller (canManage() covers MANAGE_CLIENTS role + MANAGE permission only), so a plain `return canManage();` must be graded as incorrect. Note the finding's claim about canList()==false is accurate because canList() delegates to canView(). canView(ClientModel) (line 78) already partly masked this via canConfigure(client)->canManage(client) with its all-clients fallback, so the observable defect is mainly the global canView()/canList() path.

items.defectStatement: The cleanup listener in AdminPermissions.registerListener() is now gated on Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ only. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but the older ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is not, the whole body is skipped, so role/client/group removal no longer performs permission cleanup (a regression, since the pre-change listener was ungated). When both features are enabled, management() resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2, so the ClientRemovedEvent branch calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking client deletion.
obligations: Role, client and group removal must still trigger permission cleanup whenever either ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ or ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled.

With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled (alone or together with the parent feature) the listener must not call a method that throws UnsupportedOperationException; in particular the ClientRemovedEvent branch must not invoke ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled().
Existing V1 behavior must be preserved: with only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, role/client/group removal still disables the legacy per-resource permissions.
The listener must continue to be a no-op-safe handler for unrelated events and must not throw/NPE for any removal event; it must not abort the deletion operation that fired the event.
items.notes: Note only the client branch actually reaches V2: MgmtPermissionsV2 overrides users() and clients() but not roles() or groups(), so the RoleRemovedEvent and GroupRemovedEvent branches still use legacy RolePermissions/GroupPermissions (which do not throw). Valid fixes include gating on the OR of both features and, for V2, either skipping the legacy client cleanup or routing it to a V2-appropriate path; simply changing the gate to include V2 without addressing the client branch would reintroduce the UnsupportedOperationException when both features are on. ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 lists Feature.AUTHORIZATION (not ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) as its parent, so both flags can be enabled simultaneously. The listener is registered unconditionally (DefaultKeycloakSessionFactory / QuarkusKeycloakSessionFactory), so it is the gate inside onEvent that disables cleanup. Whether the thrown exception actually propagates out of the removal call was not verified, but it is at minimum an unexpected failure on the deletion path.

items.defectStatement: ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission(String) (lines 136-144) collects resource.getName() for resources returned by resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients"), but V2 per-client resources are created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource via resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) with no setType, so their type is never "Clients" and they are not returned. The only resource whose type is "Clients" is the schema's all-clients type resource, whose name is the literal "Clients" (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init with name=type="Clients"), so the method returns either an empty set or a set containing "Clients" instead of actual client IDs. The caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions (line 229-230) feeds these values into realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream(), so it either misses all per-client grants or NPEs/ignores the bogus "Clients" entry.
obligations: The returned set must contain client identifiers that realm.getClientById(...) accepts (V2 per-client resource names are the client's ID, since AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient returns client.getId()); it must never return the literal type-resource name "Clients" or any non-client-ID string.
Clients with the requested scope granted through their per-client resource must be included; the scope match must remain exact (scope.equals(permission scope)).

A granted permission on the all-clients resource (AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)) must be honored without injecting the literal "Clients" into the result — the clients it covers (e.g. all clients of the realm) should be returned, consistent with hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) which already falls back to the all-clients resource.
Existing guards must be preserved: !root.isAdminSameRealm() and null realmResourceServer() both return an empty set, and the method must not throw for V1 vs V2 differences.
items.notes: Verified: getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema:76-114) creates per-client resources with resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner) and never calls setType; only the all-clients type resource gets setType("Clients") in init() (line 250). Valid fixes include (a) tagging per-client resources with the CLIENTS/USERS resource type inside getOrCreateResource (must cover both types and must not break getResourceTypeResource/findByName lookups), which then requires excluding/folding the type resource so the literal "Clients" is not added, or (b) not using findByType at all and deriving client IDs from the per-client resources / realm clients (V1 maps resource name to id after stripping RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX — do NOT apply the V1 "client.resource." prefix here, V2 name is already the client ID). Caller confirms values are treated as client IDs (AvailableRoleMappingResource:230). Part of finding overstated: the method is not simply "empty or polluted" always — outcome depends on whether an all-clients policy exists, but either way current output is unusable for the caller. Scope args in use are MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE / MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE.

items.defectStatement: ClientPermissionsV2.canView(ClientModel) at lines 78-79 short-circuits on the realm-wide canView() (an all-clients VIEW grant) and returns true without ever evaluating the requested client's own resource. In this class hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) treats a client-specific resource as authoritative: when a resource named by the client id exists it evaluates only that resource and ignores the all-clients resource, but canView() is satisfied by hasPermission(VIEW) against the all-clients resource alone. So an admin holding the all-clients VIEW grant is reported able to view a client that has its own resource/policy denying VIEW, and callers such as ClientsResource.getClients() (line 122/148) propagate the same global shortcut.
obligations: canView(ClientModel client) must return true only after the client-specific resource has been considered; a realm-wide ('all-clients') VIEW grant must not by itself authorize a client that has its own resource/policy denying VIEW.
