The all-clients VIEW permission must still authorize clients that have no client-specific resource, i.e. the existing hasPermission(client, VIEW) fallback to the all-clients resource (including its 'no policy attached -> false' guard) must be preserved.

Existing legitimate grants must be preserved: admins with the VIEW_CLIENTS/MANAGE_CLIENTS realm roles (canViewClientDefault) and callers that can configure/manage the client (canConfigure(client)) must still be authorized.
canView(ClientModel) must remain read-only and side-effect free, returning the same result shape (a boolean) for all callers such as RolePermissions and ClientsResource.
Do not cause clients with no per-client resource and no all-clients grant to become viewable (no fail-open regression).
items.notes: Only lines 78-79 may be replaced; a correct fix there is typically reordering to evaluate the concrete client first, e.g. keep the role/default and canConfigure(client) checks and rely on hasPermission(client, VIEW) (which already falls back to the all-clients resource only when the client has no resource of its own) instead of the realm-wide canView(). Do not 'fix' this by removing the all-clients fallback inside hasPermission(client, scope) — that fallback is needed for clients without a per-client resource. Overstated part of the finding: the global listing shortcut in ClientsResource.getClients() lives in ClientsResource lines 122/148 (via the no-arg canView()) and cannot be removed by editing the cited lines; a grader should not require the ClientsResource listing path to change as part of this hunk. Also note canConfigure(client) -> canManage(client) -> root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) or hasPermission(client, MANAGE), so MANAGE_CLIENTS is already covered; VIEW_CLIENTS (canViewClientDefault) is not, so the replacement must retain a role-based check. ClientsResource line 151 is effectively dead code (same condition already handled at 148) and is unrelated to this defect.

items.defectStatement: In `EventManager.create`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is a `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, so `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null, undefined, or empty. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, throwing a TypeError and aborting event creation instead of falling back to Cal Video (the pre-PR code used optional chaining `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and did not throw).
obligations: Accessing the first destination calendar's `integration` must not throw when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, undefined, or an empty array (guard/optional-chain required).
When location is `MeetLocationType` and there is no destination calendar (or the first one's integration is not `google_calendar`), the location must fall back to `integrations:daily` as before.
When the first destination calendar's integration is `google_calendar` and location is `MeetLocationType`, the location must NOT be overridden.
Behavior for non-Google-Meet locations must be unchanged (the fallback check only applies when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`).
items.notes: The finding is correct as stated; the only path that throws is when `evt.location === MeetLocationType` (short-circuit `&&` prevents evaluation otherwise). A correct fix is any form of null-safe read, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or an explicit guard; do not change the fallback semantics. Note the original behavior treated a missing calendar as "not google_calendar" (so it fell back to daily), which the fix must preserve. `destinationCalendar` may also be undefined, so the guard must cover that too.

items.defectStatement: In updateEvent's fallback branch (lines 254-256), the code only reaches `event.destinationCalendar?.find(...)` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined/""), yet it filters for a calendar whose `externalId === externalCalendarId` — i.e. compares against the same falsy value — so no entry can ever match and `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined. `calendar.events.update` is then called with an undefined `calendarId` (not the event's main destination calendar), regressing from the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` behavior; it does not fall back to "primary" here.
obligations: When externalCalendarId is a truthy value, selectedCalendar must still equal externalCalendarId unchanged.

When externalCalendarId is falsy/absent, selectedCalendar must resolve to the event's destination calendar externalId (e.g. the already-extracted mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId), preserving the pre-change behavior instead of yielding undefined.

The fallback must not compare candidate calendars against the falsy externalCalendarId parameter (or otherwise depend on it) — the comparison predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` must be removed/fixed.
The value passed to calendar.events.update as calendarId must remain the selected destination calendar in the fallback case; a fix must not silently keep using an undefined calendarId.
items.notes: The same erroneous pattern exists in deleteEvent (line 317): `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but there the falsy result is masked by `calendarId ? calendarId : defaultCalendarId`, so it silently falls back to "primary" rather than erroring. createEvent was fixed differently (matching `cal.credentialId === credentialId` plus `|| "primary"`); for updateEvent no credentialId argument is available, so equivalently restoring `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` or using `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` is valid. Note the finding's claim that the update "targets primary" is slightly overstated for updateEvent — an undefined calendarId produces a bogus/undefined calendar path and an API error, not a primary-calendar update; the "primary" claim is accurate for deleteEvent. Callers (CalendarManager.ts:290, EventManager.ts:542/548/586) pass possibly-null externalCalendarId despite the declared `string` type.

items.defectStatement: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts the slug spread in the organization create was inverted: it changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` (set slug directly only when team billing is disabled) to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` (set slug only when billing is enabled). As a result, with billing enabled the org is created already-published with its slug, bypassing the requestedSlug/payment publish flow, and with billing disabled no slug is set at all (org is created without a slug).
obligations: When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, the organization must be created with the `slug` field set to the input slug (direct publishing), matching the original `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` behavior.

When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, the created organization must NOT have `slug` set directly; the slug is instead carried in metadata as `requestedSlug` so the publish/payment flow assigns it later.

The metadata `requestedSlug` behavior must be preserved: `requestedSlug: slug` is included only when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, and metadata still contains isOrganization, isOrganizationVerified, isOrganizationConfigured and orgAutoAcceptEmail in both cases.
The rest of the create path (collision checks, user/membership creation, return value) must remain unchanged; no other callers or fields are affected.
items.notes: The metadata line change on cited line 153 (`IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug }` -> `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {}`) is semantically equivalent: spreading `false` yields nothing, same as `{}`, so only line 151 introduces the regression. A correct fix may restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` or use the equivalent `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`; both are valid. Note publish.handler.ts relies on metadata.requestedSlug when billing is disabled, so care should be taken that the disabled case still results in a usable org slug as before.

items.defectStatement: At packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (its type is `DestinationCalendar[] | null`). Since line 1063-1067 sets it to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, the collective team members' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped in exactly that case, so no calendar event is created on those hosts' calendars (EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterates `event.destinationCalendar`).
obligations: For a team COLLECTIVE event where both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are absent, evt.destinationCalendar must no longer remain null/undefined and must include the entries from teamDestinationCalendars, so those members' calendars are written. e.g. an array containing the team members' destination calendars.

When eventType.destinationCalendar and/or organizerUser.destinationCalendar is present, evt.destinationCalendar must still contain those entries (precedence preserved: event-type entry first, else organizer entry) followed by the collective members' destination calendars. The existing `[0]` booking connect (line ~1874-1877) must continue to point at the same primary calendar.

When there are no destination calendars at all (no event type, no organizer, no team members), evt.destinationCalendar must stay null/undefined or empty so that no booking.destinationCalendar is connected and no error is thrown; downstream `length > 0` guards must still behave as before.

The collection of teamDestinationCalendars itself must keep its current semantics: only for `isTeamEventType && schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE'`, only non-null `user.destinationCalendar`, appended once per team member.
items.notes: Confirmed against type: `destinationCalendar?: DestinationCalendar[] | null` in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:171, so `?.push` legitimately no-ops on null; the finding is accurate. Several fixes are valid, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`, `evt.destinationCalendar ??= []; evt.destinationCalendar.push(...)`, or defaulting to `[]` in the object literal at line 1063-1067. A fix that unconditionally converts null to `[]` even when teamDestinationCalendars is empty is acceptable because downstream consumers guard on `length > 0` (EventManager.ts:338, handleNewBooking.ts:1875). Do not require a specific implementation. The finding's 'hosts are not invited' phrasing is slightly loose: the concrete effect is that the collective members' calendars are not written to, since createAllCalendarEvents iterates evt.destinationCalendar.

items.defectStatement: Office365CalendarService.createEvent ignores the credentialId that CalendarManager passes (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts line 236 calls createEvent(calEvent, credential.id), and Calendar.d.ts line 221 declares the credentialId parameter), so it always picks the first entry of the event.destinationCalendar array as the target calendar. In collective/team bookings where destinationCalendar contains entries for several hosts, a co-host's event is created in the organizer's calendar ID using the co-host's token, causing the POST to /me/calendars/{externalId}/events to 404/fail. The diff only changed `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to destructuring the first array element, which is still the wrong destination when more than one destination calendar exists.
obligations: createEvent must receive and use the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager (add the second parameter, consistent with the Calendar interface in packages/types/Calendar.d.ts).

The destination calendar must be selected by matching destinationCalendar[].credentialId === credentialId (see the pattern in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), not by taking array index 0.

When a matching entry with externalId exists, POST to /me/calendars/{externalId}/events; when there is no match (or no externalId), fall back to /me/calendar/events so single-host and no-destination-calendar bookings keep working.
Preserve the existing POST body (this.translateEvent(event)), response handling (handleErrorsJson / iCalUID mapping) and error logging/rethrow.
items.notes: The finding is correct. Note the fix cannot live purely in the cited lines 73-76: the method signature on line 72 must also gain the credentialId parameter for the selection to be possible. Alternative valid implementations: inline `.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` (Google style), or a helper; a fallback to the first/primary destination calendar when no credentialId matches is acceptable as long as the credentialId match takes precedence. The array entries are DestinationCalendar objects (schema.prisma DestinationCalendar has credentialId Int?) and CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is DestinationCalendar[] | null, so `?? []` already handles the undefined/null case.

items.defectStatement: In EventManager.create(), the referencesToCreate mapping hard-codes `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so for non-calendar (dedicated video) results the credential id is always dropped. Previously the non-calendar branch used `result.credentialId`, which createMeeting()/createVideoEvent() populates with the video credential's id (videoClient.ts sets `credentialId: credential.id`); dropping it means video references are persisted without a credentialId, so later flows that need it (e.g. handleCancelBooking reads `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` to locate the credential for deleting/updating the meeting) cannot identify the video integration for that booking.
obligations: For non-calendar/video results, the produced reference's credentialId must be the id of the credential that created the video meeting (i.e. carry result.credentialId through) rather than undefined.
Calendar (isCalendarType) results must still publish credentialId (result.credentialId) and externalCalendarId (result.externalId); a fix must not regress these.
The returned value must remain type-compatible with PartialReference.credentialId (number | null | undefined) and must not add new required fields to referencesToCreate.
Persisted video references must retain their credentialId so dependent consumers (booking cancellation/update of the video integration) can look up the correct credential.
items.notes: Confirmed against the pre-change code: the old non-calendar branch was `result.credentialId`, so this is a genuine regression (not an intentional change). The finding's suggested forms `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` and plain `credentialId: result.credentialId` are equivalent, since the calendar branch already sources from result.credentialId; either is valid. Do not change externalCalendarId at line 169 — its non-calendar value was already undefined before the diff, so it is not part of the defect. Note line 209 (updateLocation) contains an analogous-looking change (`result.credentialId ?? undefined` replacing a `?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` fallback); that is a separate hunk and not required to satisfy this finding.

items.defectStatement: In the recurring/`allRemainingBookings` branch (lines 449–457) the deletion ignores the per-reference credential already resolved at lines 428–443 and instead fans out over every `_calendar` credential of the organizer, deleting only the first `_calendar` reference found in each occurrence (`find`, not `filter`). For collective bookings whose occurrences carry one calendar reference per host, only the first reference's event is deleted (co-host events survive), the same deletions are re-run for each outer reference (duplicate `deleteEvent` calls), and events can be deleted through the wrong credential because no reference/credential matching happens.
obligations: Every calendar reference of every occurrence in `updatedBookings` must be deleted through the calendar built from the credential that reference belongs to, matched by the reference's `credentialId` (not via the organizer's arbitrary/first or all calendar credentials).
All `_calendar` references of an occurrence must be handled, not only the first one matched; references written by co-hosts / other credentials (collective events) must also be deleted.
No reference may be deleted more than once: iterating the outer `bookingCalendarReference` loop must not cause duplicate `deleteEvent` calls for the same reference/occurrence.

Preserve existing behavior: non-recurring bookings still delete via the resolved reference credential; legacy references without a `credentialId` still fall back to running through all calendar credentials; deletion failures remain logged rather than thrown and the returned promises are still pushed into `apiDeletes`.
items.notes: Two valid fix shapes: (a) in the recurring branch use the already-resolved `calendar`/`calendarCredential` from lines 428–443 and, for each `updBooking`, delete refs whose `credentialId` equals that reference's `credentialId`; or (b) keep iterating credentials but use `ref.credentialId === credential.id` instead of `find(ref => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. Matching by reference `type` alone is insufficient because a user can hold multiple credentials of the same calendar type; `credentialId` is the disambiguator. Note `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` holds only the organizer's credentials, so co-host references must be resolved via the DB fallback (as lines 431–441 already do) if the fix relies on that list. The finding is accurate; the resolved `calendar` at line 443 is otherwise unused inside this branch. No test file for this handler exists.

items.defectStatement: After the change, `selectedCalendar` is derived solely from the destination-calendar entry matching `credentialId` and can now be `undefined` (`destinationCalendar` is optional and `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable). The `events.insert` call compensates with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` at line 168 still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`, so when no entry matches, the Meet/hangout-link patch is issued with an undefined `calendarId` instead of the "primary" calendar used for the insert, causing the patch to fail or target the wrong calendar.
obligations: When no destination-calendar entry matches the passed credentialId (or destinationCalendar is empty/undefined), the calendarId used for BOTH the events.insert and the subsequent events.patch must resolve to "primary" — no undefined may be sent to either Google API call.
When a matching entry (cal.credentialId === credentialId) with an externalId exists, that externalId must be used for both the insert and the patch.
The matching logic must remain by credentialId (do not reintroduce a blanket destinationCalendar.externalId lookup that ignores credentialId).
Other behavior must be preserved: conferenceDataVersion/sendUpdates options, the payload, and the resolved NewCalendarEventType return value remain unchanged.
items.notes: The defective patch call (line 168) is outside the cited 145-154 range. A valid fix can restore the fallback in the `selectedCalendar` assignment itself (e.g. `...find(...)?.externalId || "primary"`) so both downstream calls use a defined id, or introduce a resolved variable (e.g. `resolvedCalendarId`) passed to both insert and patch — either is acceptable. Trap: fixing only line 154 leaves the patch broken; the fix must ensure the patch receives the same resolved id as the insert. Out of scope for this finding: the patch call is fire-and-forget with no error handling, and the updateEvent/deleteEvent `find` against externalCalendarId changes are separate concerns.

items.defectStatement: The recurring bulk-delete block (lines 444-468) is now nested inside the per-reference loop over `bookingCalendarReference` (line 423). Because that block does not use the loop's `credentialId`/`uid`/`externalCalendarId` — it independently re-iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `updatedBookings` — it executes identically once per `_calendar` reference of `bookingToDelete`. When the cancelled booking has more than one calendar reference, the same `deleteEvent` calls for all remaining bookings are issued N times, producing duplicate API calls that fail or error.
obligations: When the booking is recurring (`eventType.recurringEvent` && `recurringEventId` && `allRemainingBookings`), the bulk deletion of every `updatedBookings` event must be performed exactly once, not once per calendar reference of `bookingToDelete` (the number of deleteEvent calls must not scale with the count of `_calendar` references).

The non-recurring path must be preserved: for each calendar reference with a `credentialId`, the referenced credential is resolved (from `user.credentials`, falling back to a DB lookup) and a single `deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` is issued for that reference.
The legacy path must be preserved: a `_calendar` reference with no `credentialId` still deletes its event through every `*_calendar` credential of the user.
Existing error handling must be kept: a failure in the bulk deletes is caught and logged rather than aborting the cancellation flow.
items.notes: The duplicate arises only when `bookingToDelete` has more than one `_calendar` reference; with a single reference there is no duplication. The inner block ignores the outer `calendar`/`uid`/`externalCalendarId` entirely and re-derives from `user.credentials` plus each updated booking's first `_calendar` reference, so either hoisting the bulk block outside the loop or gating/scoping it to the current reference fixes the cited issue. Note that `updBooking.references.find(...)` already only picks one calendar ref per booking (so multi-ref bookings are under-deleted) — that predates this change and is a separate concern. The finding's secondary claim that other hosts' events are not deleted through their own credentials is pre-existing behavior in the original single-reference code and is not introduced by this diff; it should be treated as out of scope for the graded fix. Also, whether duplicate deletes actually throw depends on the provider's idempotency, so the observable defect is duplicate API calls, not guaranteed errors.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot falls inside a date override window (dateOverrideExist is true and the `.find` did not flag the slot as outside the override), the early `return true` marks the slot available without ever running the busy-time overlap check. As a result a host who has a date override for the day but already has a conflicting booking is still reported as available.
obligations: A slot that lies within a host's date override window must still be rejected when it overlaps any entry in `busy` (the busy-time overlap check at the end of the function must run for override slots).

Date-override slots must continue to bypass the normal working-hours check (the override replaces the day's working hours), i.e. the existing intent that an override day's availability is not gated by `workingHours` must be preserved.
Slots on days with no matching date override must still be gated by both the working-hours check and the busy-time overlap check as before.
The return value semantics must remain: slots the `.find` flags as outside a same-day date override (the `return false` at line 130) and the all-busy-every logic remain unchanged.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. A valid fix removes/restructures the `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` so the working-hours block is skipped for override days but execution falls through to the final `busy.every(...)` check (e.g. guard the working-hours `if` with `!dateOverrideExist`). Simply deleting the early return would be wrong because it would then also apply the working-hours check to override days, breaking override precedence. Unrelated pre-existing bug in the same function: line 142 computes `end` identically to `start` (`hour()*60+minute()`), so working-hours end comparison is ineffective; it is out of scope for this finding and should not be required by the fix.

items.defectStatement: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114), the full-day date-override check compares two freshly constructed Dayjs objects with `===`. `dayjs(...)` returns a new object on each call, so this is reference equality and is always false: even when the adjusted override start and end denote the same instant, the branch never returns true. As a result a zero-length / full-day unavailable override is not recognized as making the slot unavailable, so the slot is incorrectly kept available.
obligations: The two timezone-adjusted values must be compared by value (instant/timestamp), not by object reference, e.g. via Dayjs `.isSame()` or comparing `.valueOf()`/`.unix()`/`.getTime()`.

When the adjusted start and end represent the same instant, the predicate callback must return true so the enclosing `dateOverrides.find(...)` truthy path makes the slot return false (unavailable), preserving the intended full-day unavailable-override behavior.

When the adjusted start and end are different instants, behavior for existing (non-zero-length) overrides must be unchanged: the subsequent `slotEndTime.isBefore/isSame(start)` and `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)` checks must still execute and control the result.
The surrounding code must not otherwise change: the utcOffset computation, the `YYYY MM DD` day match, `dateOverrideExist` handling, and the following working-hours/busy logic stay as-is.
items.notes: The defect is a genuine reference-equality bug (`===` on two distinct Dayjs objects is always false). Valid fixes include `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` or an equivalent timestamp comparison; any value-based comparison should pass. `dateOverrides` entries come from getUserAvailability (packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224) as `{start, end}` Date objects; slots.ts:410-416 adds userId/timeZone. Note: there is an unrelated pre-existing defect at slots.ts:142 (`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` rather than the slot end), which is out of scope for this finding and should not be treated as required to fix; do not let a fix for line 114 alter that block.

items.defectStatement: In the date-override branch of getSlots (packages/lib/slots.ts:216-224), the converted override bounds are reduced to a wall-clock time-of-day by `.hour()*60 + .minute()` after shifting the UTC wall time by the organizer→invitee offset. When the shifted range crosses midnight, the modulo-24h hour wraps (e.g. an organizer 20:00–23:00 override viewed from a +6h invitee tz becomes 02:00–05:00), so endTime can end up ≤ startTime (the frame is dropped by the `start >= end` check in buildSlots at line 68, yielding no slots) or the override is attributed to the wrong day. The bounds must be minutes relative to startOfInviteeDay (the same origin buildSlots uses at line 110), not time-of-day.
obligations: startTime and endTime produced for each override must be minutes measured from startOfInviteeDay (invitee-day midnight), matching the origin buildSlots applies via startOfInviteeDay.tz(inviteeTimeZone).add(minutes) at line 110; values outside 0..1439 (cross-midnight) must be preserved rather than wrapped.

For overrides whose converted range does not cross midnight, the resulting startTime/endTime must be identical to the previously computed converted invitee wall-clock time-of-day minutes (no regression for the normal case).
startTime and endTime must be derived on the same consistent basis so that a valid override satisfies endTime > startTime even when it crosses midnight after conversion.

The returned element shape must be preserved: { userIds: override.userId ? [override.userId] : [], startTime, endTime }, since the downstream splice/removal logic (lines 228-245) and buildSlots depend on userIds, startTime and endTime.
items.notes: The finding is accurate; the shift-then-modulo-24h is the actual defect. Several implementations are valid: e.g. `dayjs(override.start).tz(timeZone).diff(startOfInviteeDay, 'minute')` (and same for end), or `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset,'minute').diff(startOfInviteeDay.utc(), 'minute')`; grader should accept any fix that yields minutes-from-startOfInviteeDay. Note startOfInviteeDay = inviteeDate.startOf('day') already carries the invitee timezone, so converting override.start/end into that same tz before diffing is the natural basis. Do not over-claim: the old (pre-diff) code used raw getUTCHours/getUTCMinutes; the current offset conversion is correct for non-crossing ranges — only the modulo-24h extraction is wrong. The activeOverrides filter (line 206-207) uses dayjs.utc(override.start) against the invitee day, so it is not the subject of this finding.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable, the dateOverrides.find callback both sets dateOverrideExist as a side effect and returns true (triggering the early `return false`) as soon as the slot lies outside the current matching-day override. Because find stops at the first such override, when two or more overrides fall on the same day a slot that is contained in override A but outside the later override B makes find return truthy and the slot is wrongly rejected as unavailable, even though it is inside a valid same-day override. The containment test is being applied per-override instead of across all same-day overrides.
obligations: If a slot is contained within at least one date override whose calendar day matches the slot start day (day computed with the same organizerTimeZone offset logic), the function must treat the slot as available (return true), regardless of other same-day overrides that do not contain it.
If one or more overrides match the slot's day but the slot is contained in none of them, the slot must still be rejected (return false), preserving the current single-override behavior.

Containment boundaries must stay consistent with the existing code: a slot is outside an override when slotEndTime is before-or-equal to the override start, or slotStartTime is strictly after the override end.

When no override matches the slot's day, execution must fall through unchanged to the existing workingHours and busy checks, and the day-matching/offset computation must not change which days are considered to have overrides.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. Valid fixes include filtering the matching-day overrides first and then testing containment with `some`, or keeping find but only rejecting after checking all same-day overrides; the dateOverrideExist side-effect variable need not be preserved as long as the available/not-available outcomes above hold. Trap: the zero-length-override guard `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` is dead code (two distinct dayjs objects compare by reference, always false), so a fix may drop or repair it without regressing real behavior; graders should not require preserving its intended semantics. Separate, uncited issues in the same function: the workingHours.find predicate has the same first-match/side-effect shape and computes `end` from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime; those are outside the cited lines and need not be fixed here. Note the diff also makes overrides carry a per-availability timeZone, but this cited block keys off the organizerTimeZone parameter, so boundary/rejection behavior for single-override cases must remain as-is.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the date-override branch only detects slots that are completely disjoint from the override — slotEndTime <= override start, or slotStartTime > override end — using strict dayjs before/isSame/isAfter. It never checks that the slot actually fits inside the override, so a slot that only partially overlaps (e.g. 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 against a 10:00–11:00 override), and a slot whose start equals the override end (11:00–12:00), are treated as "within the override" and marked available.
obligations: For a slot whose date matches a date override, treat it as within the override only when slotStartTime >= override start AND slotEndTime <= override end; a slot that only partially overlaps the override (e.g. 09:30–10:30 or 10:30–11:30 for a 10:00–11:00 override) must be rejected (the not-within path must fire, making the function return false for it).
A slot whose start equals the override end (or whose end equals/falls before the override start) must be rejected as unavailable.
A slot fully contained in the override, including one exactly equal to the override interval (10:00–11:00 within a 10:00–11:00 override), must not be rejected by this override check.

Preserve the surrounding behavior: when no override matches the slot's date, dateOverrideExist stays false and evaluation falls through to the working-hours and busy checks; when an override does match and the slot is inside it, the function returns true at the dateOverrideExist guard. Keep applying the organizer-timezone offset to the override start/end as the existing code does.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. Note the boundary semantics requested: start == override start is allowed, end == override end is allowed, but start == override end must be rejected. A valid fix can replace the two disjoint checks with a containment check (e.g. reject when slotStartTime.isBefore(overrideStart) || slotEndTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)), or compute overrideStart/overrideEnd variables first; both are fine. Out of scope: line 114 compares two distinct Dayjs objects with === (always false), so its "empty override" branch never fires — a separate defect not covered by these cited lines. Also unrelated: lines 141–142 compute start and end identically, so the working-hours check is broken; do not require a fix for that here. The callback's return true still means "slot is not within this override", which the outer find/return false relies on.

items.defectStatement: In checkIfIsAvailable, the normal-working-hours guard is wrong in two ways. First, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`) instead of `slotEndTime`, so `end` always equals `start` and the `end > workingHour.endTime` bound can never fire; a slot that ends after the working-hours entry's endTime is accepted. Second, the guard uses `workingHours.find(cb)` where `cb` returns true when a given entry does NOT fully contain the slot, so the presence of any single non-containing entry makes the whole condition truthy and returns false. With multiple entries on the same day (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) the first entry that doesn't contain the slot rejects it, so essentially every slot is rejected.
obligations: The slot end (minutes since midnight, UTC) used in the working-hours comparison must be derived from slotEndTime (slot start + eventLength), not from slotStartTime, so a slot whose end exceeds a working-hour entry's endTime is rejected.

A slot must be treated as inside working hours when it is fully contained (start >= workingHour.startTime and end <= workingHour.endTime) in at least one working-hours entry whose `days` includes the slot's start day; with multiple same-day entries (e.g. 9-12 and 13-17) a slot contained in any one entry must be accepted, regardless of other non-containing entries.

A slot that is contained in no working-hours entry for its day must be rejected (return false from this block), i.e. containment must be evaluated across all entries rather than short-circuited by the first non-containing entry.
The block must only reject for the working-hours reason and otherwise fall through unchanged to the existing busy-time check below; no other behavior or return path should be altered.
items.notes: Both claims in the finding match the shown code: `end` is a copy of `start`, and `find` returning on a non-containing entry inverts the multi-entry case. The natural fix is `if (!workingHours.some(entry => entry.days.includes(day) && start >= entry.startTime && end <= entry.endTime)) return false;`. Trap to be aware of: this negated-`some` form also rejects slots on days for which there is no entry at all, and rejects everything if `workingHours` is the default empty `[]`. In this file callers spread a `schedule`/`availabilityCheckProps` that normally supplies workingHours, so empty-workingHours is an edge case; the finding's wording ("reject only if no entry on that day contains the whole slot") implies the day-with-no-entry rejection, so do not penalize that. A fix that explicitly skips the check when `workingHours.length === 0` is also defensible and acceptable as long as slots outside provided entries are still rejected. `workingHour.days`/`slotStartTime.day()` are both 0-6 day-of-week in UTC; the day-matching logic itself is not part of the defect and should be preserved.

items.defectStatement: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (slots.ts lines 138-151) the working-hours guard is inverted: `workingHours.find(cb)` returns the first entry for which `cb` returns `true`, and `cb` returns `true` when the slot lies OUTSIDE that single entry's range. The slot is therefore rejected whenever ANY applicable working-hours entry fails to contain it. When a weekday has several ranges (e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), every slot is outside at least one of them, so all slots for that day are rejected and hosts with split working days lose their availability. The slot must be rejected only when NO applicable range (a `workingHours` entry whose `days` include the slot's weekday) contains it. (The `end` variable is also computed from `slotStartTime`, identical to `start`, so the slot's real end is never validated — see notes.)
obligations: A slot whose time lies within at least one workingHours entry whose `days` include the slot's weekday must be treated as available (the guard must not return false), including when that weekday has multiple ranges and the slot only fits one of them.
A slot that lies outside every applicable workingHours entry for its weekday must still be rejected (guard returns false), as before for single-range days.
The applicability condition must stay day-scoped: entries whose `days` do not include the slot's weekday must not influence the result (they must not cause acceptance by omission nor rejection).

Everything else in `checkIfIsAvailable` must keep working unchanged: the currentSeats early-return true, the dateOverrides logic and its early returns, and the busy-times check; only the working-hours guard logic may change.
items.notes:
- Valid fixes: negate the `find` callback so it locates a containing range and reject only if none is found, or switch to `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`. Both are equivalent; exact predicate boundary semantics (a slot starting exactly at startTime or ending exactly at endTime is inside, matching the existing `<`/`>` comparisons) should be preserved.
- Trap: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates `start`, so the pre-existing code never checked the slot's end against the range. This is a separate, pre-existing defect not described by the finding; a fix may leave it or correctly use `slotEndTime` — either passes the obligations above, but the grader should not treat keeping it as a regression.
- Trap: `workingHours` defaults to `[]`, and the seated/reserved-slot caller around line 581 spreads only `availabilityCheckProps` (no `workingHours`), so a bare `!some(...)` makes that path reject every slot, whereas the old `find`-based code was permissive when the list was empty. Also, entries whose `days` do not match previously left the slot accepted. A guard such as `workingHours.length && !some(...)` preserves the old permissive behavior; both variants satisfy the obligations.
- Pre-existing, out of scope: the weekday is taken from `slotStartTime.day()` (UTC) while workingHours days are localized to the user's timezone; the timezone/day mismatch is not part of this finding.

items.defectStatement: In scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 53-77, a single try/catch wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop. Because `client.request` is awaited inside the loop, any SendGrid failure (e.g. a 4xx for an already-sent/already-cancelled batch_id) throws, aborts the loop, skips all remaining reminders' cancel+delete, and skips `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` so deletes already collected are never awaited. Since these reminders belong to cancelled/rescheduled bookings and SendGrid has already accepted the scheduled send, the untouched ones still get delivered — the exact "reminders of cancelled bookings are still sent" bug the PR targets.
obligations: A failure cancelling/deleting one reminder must not prevent the remaining reminders in remindersToCancel from being processed (loop must continue past a per-item error).

For each reminder a correct fix must still attempt the SendGrid cancel (POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends with batch_id=referenceId, status cancel) and delete the WorkflowReminder row by id, preserving current ordering/arguments.

Errors must still be caught and logged (e.g. per-item try/catch or Promise.allSettled) so the handler does not throw and the subsequent unscheduled-reminder scheduling (lines 79+) still runs and returns 200.
Collected prisma delete promises must actually be awaited (Promise.all) or each delete awaited inline, independent of whether the per-item SendGrid call succeeded.
items.notes: Finding is accurate. Valid fixes: per-item try/catch around the request+delete; or await each delete inline inside a try/catch; or keep the array but await it after/independent of the loop using Promise.allSettled and log rejections. Note a nuance the finding glosses over: if the SendGrid cancel fails, deleting the row removes it from future retries, whereas leaving it (cancelled:true) lets the next cron run retry the cancel — a fix that deletes-first or skips delete on cancel failure is still defensible as long as one failure does not abort the rest. Rows with null referenceId are possible in principle; manager code (deleteScheduledEmailReminder) guards for null, this inline code does not, but that is out of scope for this finding. The prisma delete was previously reached only after a successful request, so the fix should not silently change which rows get deleted beyond continuing on error.

items.defectStatement: In deleteScheduledSMSReminder (packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177-186) the prisma.workflowReminder.delete for reminderId is placed inside the same try block immediately after `await twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)`, so if the Twilio cancel rejects, the delete is never reached and the workflowReminder row is left behind with no cancelled flag and no retry, even though the booking/step that owned it is gone.
obligations: The prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } }) must still be executed for the given reminderId even when twilio.cancelSMS throws (deletion must not be gated on Twilio success).
When referenceId is null/absent, no Twilio call is made but the DB row must still be deleted (preserve the current null guard).
When referenceId is present, twilio.cancelSMS must still be attempted (cancellation behavior preserved).
The function must not throw to its callers on either Twilio or Prisma failure; errors should continue to be caught and logged as before (callers invoke it unawaited inside forEach loops).
items.notes: Valid fixes: move the prisma delete into a finally (or outside the Twilio try), or catch the Twilio error separately and proceed; the row could alternatively be marked deleted/cancelled, but plain deletion matches this function's existing contract. Trap: the finding's "WHY" history is inaccurate — before this diff the function only called cancelSMS and performed no DB delete at all, so no prior caller-side deletion existed; the added delete is new, and the real defect is purely its coupling to Twilio success. Note referenceId is @unique in the WorkflowReminder model, so leaving rows undeleted can also keep stale unique referenceIds around. Callers (handleCancelBooking.ts:490, handleNewBooking.ts:970, bookings.tsx:492, workflows.tsx:216/380/523/578) pass (reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) and do not delete the row themselves, confirming the manager is now solely responsible for the DB delete.

items.defectStatement: In the catch block (lines 189–196), the retry counter is updated with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, a read-modify-write using the value read when the reminder list was fetched. If two handler runs (e.g. overlapping cron invocations) process the same reminder, each computes the increment from the same snapshot and the later write clobbers the earlier, undercounting retries. The update should be an atomic increment instead.
obligations: The catch-block update increments retryCount by exactly one against the current DB value (e.g. Prisma `{ increment: 1 }`), rather than assigning `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the in-memory snapshot.
The update is still scoped `where: { id: reminder.id }` and only sets retryCount, preserving the existing behavior of recording a failed scheduling attempt.
The catch block still catches the error and logs it (`console.log(...)`) and does not rethrow or alter the response, so a failed reminder does not abort processing of the remaining reminders.
No change to how retryCount is selected/cast in this file is required for the fix; `reminder.retryCount` may no longer be read if an atomic increment is used.
items.notes: The same stale-read pattern exists in the else branch at line 184 (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`); a complete fix treats them identically, but the graded replacement is only for the cited lines 189–196. The claimed race requires concurrent/overlapping invocations of this endpoint; within a single sequential run each reminder is processed once, so the finding is somewhat overstated, but the atomic increment is still the correct form. A valid alternative is a raw `{ increment: 1 }` update; any equivalent atomic DB-side increment is acceptable. Do not mark removing the `retryCount` selection as required.

items.defectStatement: The catch block in the per-reminder loop performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update`. If that update itself throws — e.g. the reminder row was already removed by the handler's own cleanup/deleteMany or a concurrent cron run (Prisma P2025), or a transient DB error occurs — the error escapes the catch, terminates the `for` loop, and the remaining unscheduled reminders are never processed (it propagates to `defaultHandler`, which returns a 500).
obligations: A failure in the error-recovery step (the retryCount write, or the logging) must not stop the loop from continuing to process the remaining reminders. The error path must not rethrow out of the loop iteration.

On the error path the reminder's retryCount must still be incremented when the row exists, preserving the existing behavior that lets the cleanup delete/stop retrying failed SMS reminders (retryCount > 1).
The original scheduling error must still be logged/reported.
The success path (scheduled update with scheduled:true/referenceId, the else-branch retryCount update, and the rest of the loop) must be unchanged.
items.notes: The handler is wrapped by defaultHandler's try/catch (packages/lib/server/defaultHandler.ts), so the throw yields a 500 response rather than crashing the process, but it still aborts the batch — the finding's core claim holds. Note the finding's alternative suggestion "move the log before the update" is insufficient on its own: the update would still throw and abort the loop; a guard (own try/catch) or a non-throwing write is required. A valid alternative is `updateMany` with `where: { id: reminder.id }`, which returns count 0 instead of throwing when the row is gone. Either way, do not let the recovery write halt processing. Only the cited catch block (lines ~189-197) is in scope; unrelated issues (e.g. the deleteMany `retryCount > 1` clause not being scoped to SMS method) are out of scope.

items.defectStatement: The newly added `else` branch (lines 178-186) treats any falsy return from `twilio.scheduleSMS` as a send failure and increments `retryCount`. But `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` exactly when SMS sending is locked (`isLockedForSMSSending`, twilioProvider.ts:90-95), so a temporary user/team SMS lock is recorded as a retry; combined with the top-level `deleteMany` clause `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`, the still-valid reminder is permanently deleted a run or two later instead of being retried once the lock is lifted.
obligations: When `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value (the locked/skipped path), `retryCount` must NOT be incremented (the reminder keeps its prior retryCount, e.g. 0), so it does not become a deletion candidate via `deleteMany({ retryCount: { gt: 1 } })`.
The reminder must remain eligible for a later retry: `scheduled` stays false and `scheduledDate`/`referenceId` are unchanged, so the next cron run re-fetches and re-attempts it.
Genuine send failures (the `catch` block) must still increment `retryCount` as before, so real errors are still bounded by the retry limit.
Successful scheduling (`scheduledSMS` truthy) must still set `scheduled: true` and `referenceId: scheduledSMS.sid`, unchanged.
items.notes: `scheduleSMS` (twilioProvider.ts:79-114) is the only source of a falsy result here; aside from the lock early-return it returns the Twilio message object (truthy) or throws (handled by catch), so the `else` branch effectively fires only for the lock/skip case. Valid fixes include simply removing the increment from the `else` (do nothing / leave it unscheduled) or having the caller distinguish the locked/skipped result before touching retryCount; do not add a different counter or mark it scheduled. Scope: the fix belongs in the cited `else` branch — the catch-block increment must be preserved. Note the top-level `deleteMany` OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, so it also deletes non-SMS reminders; that is a separate defect outside the cited lines. The finding's "after two cron runs" is approximate: the increment happens on runs 1 and 2 and deletion occurs on the following deleteMany pass.

items.defectStatement: At line 97, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success, data }`), but the whole object is assigned to `key` and persisted to `prisma.credential.update` as `data: { key }`. This stores the wrapper (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`) instead of the parsed credential object, so the next time this credential is used, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 fails because `scope`/`token_type`/`expiry_date`/`access_token`/`refresh_token` are no longer at the top level — permanently breaking the Google Calendar credential after the first token refresh.
obligations: The value persisted in `credential.key` (line 100) must be the parsed credential object itself (top-level `scope`, `token_type`, `expiry_date`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`), not the `SafeParseReturnType` wrapper.

The refreshed `access_token` and `expiry_date` (set on `googleCredentials` at lines 95-96) must still be included in the persisted key, and the credential parse must still throw/abort persistence when parsing fails (existing behavior from the helper's throw).
A subsequent instantiation of `GoogleCalendarService` with the updated credential must pass `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75.
The update call itself and which credential is updated (`where: { id: credential.id }`) must be unchanged.
items.notes: Valid fixes: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data;` or reverting to `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (which returns the parsed object directly and throws on failure). The helper already throws `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"` on `!success`, so adding a `.success` check is unnecessary. Note the other callers (zoomvideo, office365calendar, salesforce) correctly use `.data`/`.success`; only this googlecalendar call is wrong. Only line 97 needs changing — lines 98-100 are correct.

items.defectStatement: On line 31, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError when the request body is valid JSON but does not match the schema (e.g. missing/incorrectly-typed `userId`, `appSlug`, or `keys`). The handler has no try/catch around it, so the error propagates and Next.js responds with 500 instead of a 400 client-error.
obligations: A request body that fails schema validation must yield an HTTP 400 response and must not let an exception (ZodError) escape the handler.

A body that passes validation must continue through the existing flow unchanged: userId/appSlug/keys extraction, user lookup (404), app lookup (404), decrypt, and the credential update/create responses.
The existing pre-validation guards must stay in place and precede validation: disabled credential sharing => 403, and non-matching webhook secret => 403.
The fix must not alter the schema's accepted shape (userId integer, appSlug string, keys string) or the success responses/messages.
items.notes: Any 400-on-invalid-body behavior is acceptable (safeParse with a 400 return, or try/catch around parse); the exact error message/body is not part of the contract. Note the finding slightly overstates "malformed body": a syntactically invalid JSON body is already rejected by Next's body parser before the handler runs, so the real 500 case is a parseable-but-schema-invalid body. The same file also has other unguarded throws after this line (JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on a bad/undecryptable `keys`, and prisma create/update errors) which can also 500; they are outside the cited line and not required by this fix.

items.defectStatement: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (lines 25-27) the code unconditionally assigns the literal `"refresh_token"` to `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` whenever the parsed response lacks one, regardless of which parse branch was taken. In the non-sharing branch this corrupts flows whose caller schema marks `refresh_token` optional: office365calendar parses with `refreshTokenResponseSchema` (refresh_token optional, CalendarService.ts:56) and then does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` (CalendarService.ts:264) before persisting, so when the provider's refresh response omits `refresh_token` the placeholder overwrites the still-valid stored refresh token, making the next refresh send `refresh_token="refresh_token"` and fail permanently. The prior raw `schema.safeParse` path did not mutate the data, so the old token was preserved.
obligations: In the sharing/sync path (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` && `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, using `minimumTokenResponseSchema`), the returned data must still contain a `refresh_token` placeholder when the sync response omits one, preserving existing behavior for that flow.

In the non-sharing path (caller-provided schema), when the parsed response omits `refresh_token` the function must not add one to the returned data, so callers that spread the result over stored credentials (office365calendar) keep their existing refresh token.
A `refresh_token` that is present in the parsed response must never be overwritten in either branch.

Preserve the existing return contract and error behavior: return the successful `safeParse`-shaped result (`success` plus `data`) and still throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` on parse failure, without breaking the zoomvideo, googlecalendar, or salesforce callers.
items.notes: Main affected caller is office365calendar (optional refresh_token + spread over the stored key). salesforce re-adds the stored token explicitly (CalendarService.ts:98) and zoomvideo requires refresh_token in its schema, so neither is broken by the current code; googlecalendar passes credentials that already include refresh_token. The finding's suggestion is one valid approach (restrict the placeholder to the minimumTokenResponseSchema branch) but any fix that avoids introducing/overwriting refresh_token in the non-sharing branch while keeping the sharing-path placeholder is acceptable — do not require a specific signature/flag. Grader should treat "only mutate in the sharing branch" and "only inject when the caller's schema requires refresh_token" as equally correct.

items.defectStatement: In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`, the new refresh block unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with Cal.com's own `consumer_key`/`consumer_secret`, bypassing `refreshOAuthTokens`; so when credential sharing is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` + `credential.userId`) the external sync endpoint is ignored. It also decides success with `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of `response.ok`, so a valid 2xx response over HTTP/2 (empty statusText) throws an HttpError, and it refreshes and writes to the DB on every service construction rather than only when the access token is missing/expired.
obligations: The token refresh must go through refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFn, "salesforce", credential.userId) (or equivalent) so that when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId is set, the external sync endpoint is used instead of Cal.com's own consumer credentials.

Success must be determined by HTTP status (e.g. response.ok / res.ok), not response.statusText; an empty statusText on a 2xx response must not be treated as an error, while genuine non-2xx failures must still surface as an error.

The refresh and the prisma.credential.update must run only when the stored access token is missing or expired; when a usable stored access_token exists, getClient must skip the network call and DB write and use the stored token.

The response must still be parsed via parseRefreshTokenResponse and the updated tokens (preserving the stored refresh_token and instance_url) persisted to the credential, with getClient returning a jsforce.Connection configured from the resulting access token/instance_url so subsequent salesforce operations keep working.
items.notes: parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on an invalid token response (and switches to minimumTokenResponseSchema when credential sharing is on), so the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is effectively dead; a fix may keep or remove it. The salesforceTokenSchema has no numeric expiry (only issued_at), so "expired" may be undeterminable; refreshing only when access_token is absent is a reasonable interpretation. getClient is memoized in the constructor, so the extra round trip/DB write happens once per SalesforceCalendarService instance, not per API method call. Several valid fixes exist (mirroring the zoomvideo/office365calendar pattern); the grader should accept any that satisfies the obligations above.

items.defectStatement: In addGuestsHandler the authorization flag is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, which requires the user to be both admin and owner. Since isTeamOwner is only true for OWNER role, a plain team ADMIN (who is not an OWNER) evaluates to false, so the booking authorization check at line 54 wrongly rejects admins with FORBIDDEN. The sibling handlers (confirm.handler.ts:127, teams/get.handler.ts:48) correctly treat admin-or-owner as a disjunction. Note isTeamAdmin already returns true for both ADMIN and OWNER roles, so with `||` the second call is effectively redundant but harmless.
obligations: A team ADMIN who is not a team OWNER must be treated as authorized (isTeamAdminOrOwner truthy).
A team OWNER must remain authorized (isTeamAdminOrOwner truthy).
A user who is neither admin nor owner, not the booking organizer, and not an attendee must still be rejected with the FORBIDDEN 'you_do_not_have_permission' error.

Behavior for bookings without a team (booking.eventType?.teamId null/undefined, defaulted to 0) must remain unauthorized via the team-role path, i.e. no crash and no false positive from the team check.
The existing organizer and attendee authorization paths must be preserved.
items.notes: The finding is correct; the code as shown is the defect. Valid fixes: change `&&` to `||`, or compute membership.role comparison as in confirm.handler.ts. Note isTeamAdmin returns the membership object (or false), not a boolean, but it is truthy-checked so it does not affect correctness. Using `||` makes the isTeamOwner call redundant because isTeamAdmin already covers ADMIN and OWNER; a fix that simply drops the isTeamOwner call and keeps isTeamAdmin would also be correct, so do not require both functions be retained. Grading should focus on ADMIN being admitted while unauthorized users are still rejected.

items.defectStatement: ZAddGuestsInputSchema only validates that each entry of `guests` is an email; it does not enforce uniqueness, so a client that sends the same address twice in one request passes validation. The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only removes emails already present on the booking or blacklisted, not duplicates within the submitted array, so `createMany` inserts duplicate attendee records.
obligations: Duplicate emails within the submitted `guests` array must not result in duplicate attendee records server-side (either rejected during parsing or deduplicated before persistence).
Valid unique email arrays must still parse successfully, and each string must remain email-validated (z.string().email()).
The shape/inferred type must stay compatible with callers: bookingId remains a number and TAddGuestsInputSchema still exposes `guests` as a string array usable by the handler and sendAddGuestsEmails.
Existing behavior for the single-guest and non-duplicate cases (including the handler's filter against already-present attendees / blacklisted emails) must remain intact.
items.notes: The fix location is not unique: a valid alternative is to dedupe in the handler before building guestsFullDetails (e.g. a Set over uniqueGuests); the schema-level .refine()/.transform() suggested by the finding is also valid. Findings slightly overstate that nothing checks uniqueness: the web client (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29) already refines for unique emails, but that is only client-side and not a server boundary. Keep in mind that a .transform() changes the inferred output type, so a refine-based rejection or handler-side dedupe may be safer for type compatibility; note that after a failed refine the handler's "emails_must_be_unique_valid" path is unaffected.

items.defectStatement: In addGuests.handler.ts lines 70-77, the blacklist check compares the raw guest string against lowercased blacklist entries (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so an authorized caller can invite a blocked address by changing letter case (user@x.com vs User@X.com) or by using a plus-alias (blocked+anything@x.com), bypassing the base-email normalization that handleNewBooking/checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked apply. A correct fix normalizes each guest with extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() before the blacklist comparison, mirroring the existing pattern in handleNewBooking.ts lines 741-746.
obligations: Each guest is compared against the blacklist after base-email extraction and lowercasing (e.g. extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()), so case variants and plus-aliases of a blacklisted address are rejected; case-insensitivity of the blacklist entries themselves is preserved.

The blacklist filter only removes matching guests from the list to be added; non-blacklisted guests must still pass through and be added (and the same-email de-duplication against booking.attendees must be preserved), keeping the existing behavior that an all-filtered-out list throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'.
When BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is unset/empty, no guest is blocked (empty list short-circuits as before).

extractBaseEmail must be imported/available in addGuests.handler.ts and the email values stored/created for guests (guestsFullDetails) must remain the original guest addresses, not the normalized base form.
items.notes: The cited finding is accurate: handleNewBooking.ts (lines 742-743) and checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts both compare extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase() against blacklist entries lowercased, so this handler is inconsistent. A fix may normalize either the guest or the blacklist entries (or both); the key is a normalized, case-insensitive, plus-stripped comparison. Trap: do not change the stored attendee email to the base address — only the comparison should be normalized. Note the pre-existing same-email dedup check (guest === attendee.email) is separate and not part of this finding.

items.defectStatement: In addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-78, the guest filter compares the raw input guest against (a) `attendee.email` case-sensitively and (b) `blacklistedGuestEmails`, which was already lowercased at lines 70-72 — so the blacklist comparison can never match an uppercase/mixed-case guest. Result: a blacklisted email typed in different case bypasses the filter, and an attendee already on the booking can be re-added with different casing. Neither the input schema nor the dialog normalizes casing before this handler.
obligations: The duplicate check against existing attendees must be case-insensitive (e.g. compare lowercased guest to lowercased attendee.email), so a guest whose email differs only in case from an existing attendee is filtered out.
The blacklist check must be case-insensitive against the already-lowercased blacklistedGuestEmails list, so a blacklisted email in any casing is filtered out.

The original casing of accepted guests must be preserved for persistence/emails: guestsFullDetails and the email/calendar flow must still use the guest string as supplied (do not lowercase the stored email).
When every supplied guest is filtered out (duplicate or blacklisted), the handler must still throw the BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error as before.
items.notes: Only the comparison logic on lines 74-78 needs changing; lowercasing both sides is valid, as is precomputing a lowercased attendee set. Not in scope / do not overstate: the filter only compares against booking.attendees, so duplicates within the input `guests` array itself are not deduped (same as before; the dialog tries client-side dedup); the blacklist here does not use extractBaseEmail like checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts/handleNewBooking.ts do, and the fix is not required to add it. `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the unfiltered `guests` array — a separate pre-existing behavior, not part of this finding.

items.defectStatement: In CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx (lines 42-50), `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional parent `onSuccess`; it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. When the parent does not refetch (e.g. EventAdvancedTab renders the wrapper without an `onChanged`/`onSuccess` prop, and the dropdown still renders for Google calendars with a cache), the dropdown keeps showing the stale `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful cache deletion. The sibling `disconnectMutation` (lines 53-65) already invalidates `connectedCalendars` (and `apps.integrations`) in `onSettled`, which this mutation lacks.
obligations: After a successful `deleteCache` mutation, `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` must be invalidated so the connectedCalendars query (and therefore `cacheUpdatedAt`) is refetched.
The existing success toast (`cache_deleted_successfully`) on success and error toast (`error_deleting_cache`) on failure must be preserved.

The parent `onSuccess` callback must still be invoked on success, and the existing `disconnectMutation` behavior (toast, onSuccess, invalidation of connectedCalendars and apps.integrations) must not regress.
Invalidation must be tied to the deleteCache mutation's outcome (only refetch after a successful delete); any promise returned from invalidation should be awaited/handled rather than left dangling.
items.notes: The finding is accurate. Blast radius: two callers pass `onSuccess`/`onChanged` via SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper — CalendarListContainer.tsx (its `onChanged` already invalidates connectedCalendars + apps.integrations, so the staleness is masked there) and EventAdvancedTab.tsx, which passes no `onChanged` at all, so nothing refetches and the bug manifests. Valid fixes include adding an `async onSuccess`/`onSettled` to `deleteCacheMutation` that invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`; note `const utils = trpc.useUtils()` is declared after line 42, but the callbacks run after render so referencing it is safe (moving it up is also acceptable). No need to invalidate `apps.integrations`, since the credential is not removed here.

items.defectStatement: In the reschedule handler, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) / deleteMeeting(...) })` gives `forEach` an async callback whose returned promises are discarded. Nothing awaits the calendar/video deletions, so execution continues to `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and the `BOOKING_CANCELLED` webhooks before the old event/meeting is actually deleted, and any rejection from `getCalendar`/`deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection (the added `await` inside the callback alone does not fix this).
obligations: The calendar/video deletions for all entries in bookingRefsFiltered must be awaited (or otherwise observed) so that the handler does not proceed to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks until the deletions have settled; a Promise.all over a .map of async callbacks, a for...of with await, etc. are all acceptable.

The per-reference logic must be preserved: only refs whose type exists in credentialsMap are processed; refs without uid are skipped; *_calendar refs use getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(type)) awaited and then calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, builder.calendarEvent, bookingRef.externalCalendarId); *_video refs call deleteMeeting(credentialsMap.get(type), uid).
Rejections from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting must not be left unobserved — they must either propagate (so the mutation fails) or be caught/logged deliberately, rather than silently dropped.
getCalendar must still be awaited since it returns a Promise<Calendar | null> (the callback may legitimately handle a null calendar).
items.notes: The finding is accurate; the only in-diff change on this line made the callback async/awaited getCalendar but left forEach unawaited. Primary intended fix: `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`. Note the tradeoff: a plain Promise.all changes behavior so that one failing deletion aborts the reschedule email/webhook; a per-ref .catch is an equally valid fix if keeping the rest of the flow alive is desired. Graders should accept sequential for...of as well. The nearby line 964 `await appStore[...]` is a separate unrelated change and not part of this finding. Note bookingRefsFiltered already filters to refs with credentials, so the credentialsMap.get() inside is non-null in practice.

items.defectStatement: In packages/app-store/index.ts the object literal eagerly evaluates `import("./x")` for every app at module-load time, so merely importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading of all app modules (Google Calendar, Stripe, Salesforce, etc.). Converting the static `import * as x` bindings into dynamic `import()` values only changes the map values to Promises; it does not defer loading, so the intended laziness is not achieved.
obligations: Module loading must be deferred until an app entry is actually requested: no `import()` may be invoked while the `appStore` object is being constructed/evaluated at module load.

Existing consumers must keep functioning. Call sites do `const app = await appStore[key]` and then use `app.lib.CalendarService` / `app.lib.VideoApiAdapter` (getCalendar.ts:15, videoClient.ts:26, deletePayment.ts:16, handlePayment.ts:26, bookings.tsx:967, handleCancelBooking.ts:589); the resolved value must still be the app's module namespace object containing `lib`.

The set of keys and their naming must be preserved (including `sylapsvideo`, `wipemycalother`, etc.) so `keyof typeof appStore` lookups used by callers still type-check, and `export default appStore` must remain the default export.

Unknown/absent keys must still resolve to undefined (callers guard with `app && "lib" in app`) without throwing; if the map value becomes a thunk/callback, all use sites must be updated to invoke it (e.g. `await appStore[key]?.()`).
items.notes: Trap: wrapping entries in thunks alone is insufficient and actually breaks callers — every use site (`packages/core/videoClient.ts:26`, `packages/app-store/_utils/getCalendar.ts:15`, `packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts:16`, `packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts:26`, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:967`, `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:589`) currently does a bare `await appStore[key]` without calling. A thunk-based fix must also update those sites to call the thunk; a Proxy/lazy-getter approach can defer the `import()` while keeping the `await appStore[key]` call sites unchanged and returning the module namespace. Both are valid as long as loading is deferred. Note appStore keys only cover the ~28 listed apps; other apps (e.g. `_appRegistry`, `utils.ts`, `locations.ts`) use `appStoreMetadata`, not this map, so they are unaffected. The `// example: import("./example")` comment line is inert and can be left or adjusted.

items.defectStatement: TotalDocs at pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:146 iterates the b.cache map without holding cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache under cacheMu.Lock() at line 137-139 (and GetIndex reads it under RLock). Concurrent map read during Prometheus collection therefore races with the map write; it must take the read lock (cacheMu.RLock/RUnlock) around the iteration.
obligations: TotalDocs must synchronize access to b.cache (e.g. acquire cacheMu.RLock before the range loop and release it before returning) so the map iteration cannot race with BuildIndex's write.
TotalDocs must preserve existing behavior: sum DocCount() over every cached index, skip indices whose DocCount returns an error, and return the total as int64.

Existing locking in GetIndex (RLock) and BuildIndex (Lock only around the map assignment) must remain intact; a correct fix must not reintroduce a coarse lock held during builder execution or otherwise change their semantics.
The fix must not deadlock or call DocCount while a lock that BuildIndex needs is held in a way that blocks the write path indefinitely (a read lock held for the loop is acceptable).
items.notes: The finding is essentially correct and the fix (RLock) matches the existing GetIndex pattern. Slight overstatement: before this PR BuildIndex held cacheMu.Lock for its whole body but TotalDocs still read the map without any lock, so the map read/write race already existed; the finer-grained locking does not invent it, though the write window relative to other work differs. Either way the required fix is to add read-locking to TotalDocs. DocCount is a bleve index call; holding RLock across it is fine and does not conflict with the writer lock. Only two methods touch b.cache (BuildIndex writer, GetIndex/TotalDocs readers); no other unprotected access exists.

items.defectStatement: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire build, which serialized builds of all keys; the change moved locking to wrap only the final cache write (b.cache[key] = idx at lines 137-139). This removes the coarse serialization but also removes any mutual exclusion per key, so two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource both call bleve.New on the same directory (filepath.Join(Root, Namespace, Resource.Group)), both run the builder/ListIterator+Write+Flush, and both do cache[key]=idx with a last-wins clobber and a doubled IndexTenants.Inc.
obligations: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource key must be mutually exclusive (or deduplicated) so the builder and bleve.New/Flush run only once per key for a given build.
Builds for different keys must still be able to proceed concurrently; do not reintroduce a single coarse lock held across the whole build.
The cache write b.cache[key]=idx must remain correct and race-free (still synchronized), and BuildIndex must still return the built index, or an equivalent already-built index, for the requested key.
Error paths must be preserved: a failed build must not leave a partial/stale entry in the cache and must still return the error, and subsequent callers must be able to retry.
items.notes: The finding is accurate and matches the diff: the deleted code was a single cacheMu.Lock/defer Unlock spanning the whole function, i.e. global (not per-key) exclusion. Valid fixes include singleflight.Group keyed by NamespacedResource, a per-key lock/mutex map, or re-checking the cache before/after building; all are acceptable. The search.go getOrCreateIndex already has a TODO acknowledging the desire to block only for the same key and to return the same index. Grader should not require a specific mechanism, only that same-key builds cannot run concurrently/double and different-key builds remain parallel. Note the cache holds *bleveIndex; if a dedup approach returns an already-cached index, the metric IndexTenants.Inc should not be double-counted for the same build.

items.defectStatement: In `RuleActionsButtons.V2` the "Silence notifications" menu item is enabled from the Grafana prom rule's abilities (`AlertRuleMenu` computes `canSilence` via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), but the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (line 104). In the new list view the component is rendered with only `promRule` and `rule` is undefined (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` passes `promRule={rule}` with no `rule`), so `handleSilence`'s `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)` never renders a drawer and the click is a no-op.
obligations: When the component is rendered with only `promRule` (list view) and the prom rule is a Grafana alerting rule, clicking Silence must actually open the silence drawer instead of doing nothing.

The drawer must receive a usable Grafana rule uid for the clicked rule (derived from the provided `promRule` when `rule` is absent) so the silences editor targets the correct rule; `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` must not be given an undefined `rulerRule` (its memo comparator reads `rulerRule.grafana_alert.uid`).

Existing behavior must be preserved: when `rule` is a `RulerGrafanaRuleDTO`, Silence still opens the drawer as before, and non-Grafana / non-alerting (e.g. recording or datasource) rules still do not render the drawer.
The component must continue to render/return without crashing or throwing when `rule` is undefined (e.g. the early `!identifier` return and clone-redirect paths keep working).
